LOWPRICE.rationale: This is a 34-35% EBITDA margin business protected by ALMM/DCR domestic-content rules, running at only 43-45% module utilisation — the opposite of the low-margin, high-asset-turn model; cost talk is generic ('cost competitiveness') with no itemised savings or cost culture described.
LOWPRICE.quote: at Emmvee we are very much geared up with the cost competitiveness

PRICING.rationale: Management explicitly describes structural price deflation over its history and flat realisations now (15-16 cents/watt non-DCR, EBITDA/watt 'not much' changed Q4 to Q1); the margin uplift comes from DCR policy mix and internal cell consumption, not from raising prices.
PRICING.quote: When we started the price was three Euros per watt. And today we are talking about less than 5% of what it was back then

BRAND.rationale: There is a genuine three-decade quality record used as a B2B credential — warranty claim rate <0.008% over three years and a claim to sit 'at the top of the evaluation matrix' for developers — but no A&P spend, no premium pricing from the name, and no adjacency stretch; realisations track the commodity.
BRAND.quote: Emmvee's warranty claim rate... was less than 0.008% for the average of last three years... So these are certain things where Emmvee is put at the top of the evaluation matrix

INNOVATION.rationale: Early and full TOPCon adoption, 100% module capacity converted, and the G12R transition are real technology-timing wins, and a process-R&D team with PhDs is claimed — but when directly asked for R&D spend and its five-year growth the CEO had no numbers, and the technology is bought-in equipment rather than proprietary R&D dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: without having numbers in front of me, what I will talk about is... we have recently moved into TopCon cell manufacturing

FORWARD.rationale: Emmvee is moving in the opposite direction — backward into cells now and ingots/wafers by FY29-30 — with no own stores, franchising, D2C or licensing anywhere in the three calls; even exports are explicitly treated as optional upside rather than a channel build.
FORWARD.quote: we intend to set up an ingot and wafer facility of about 9 gigawatt integrating us fully in phases

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volumes and order book grew persistently (module production 1,482MW to 2,999MW; order book 4.9GW to 9.4GW to 9.9GW; top-10 average order size 121MW to 221MW), which implies share gain in a fragmented industry where only 26GW of 82GW capacity actually produced — but management never gives an explicit market-share number or names competitors, and exports were zero in FY26.
SHAREGAIN.quote: The average order size among the top 10 customers increased to 221 megawatt in FY26 compared to 121 megawatt in FY25

CULTURE.rationale: The short listed record shows promises kept: IPO proceeds used exactly as stated (INR1,621cr prepaid, net debt/equity -0.06x, ICRA upgraded BBB- to A), both 2.5GW module lines commissioned on the announced schedule, and the 6GW project tracking to guided dates. Against that, only three calls exist, no mistake or bad news has yet been owned, and the R&D question was deflected — too little history to call it strong.
CULTURE.quote: we have repaid a total of 1,621 crores from the IPO proceeds... net debt to equity stood at negative 0.06x

MOATTEST.rationale: The articulated barriers — Class 6 cleanrooms, 14-step TOPCon vs 8-step PERC, ALMM listing — are capital and permitting hurdles that Emmvee itself cleared in about two years and is replicating for INR5,500cr, in an industry already carrying 82GW of module capacity against 26GW of domestic production. The advantage rests on government DCR/ALMM policy rather than anything a funded entrant could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: with a 82 gigawatt of installed capacity of modules last year, India imported 15 gigawatt of modules... bringing it to 26 gigawatt of modules only that was manufactured by Indian manufacturers

RECURRING.rationale: There is no licence, subscription, AMC or deferred-revenue model; the only annuity-like stream is replacement/aftermarket parts riding on the installed base of vehicles carrying Endurance components, which management repeatedly flags as a strategic priority (37 export countries, target of 10% of India sales by FY28), but attach rates, renewals and customer advances are never discussed.
RECURRING.quote: our focus is to reach 10% of India sales by FY28. In Q1 FY25, aftermarket sales grew by 14.94%

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Genuine middleman economics exist only in the aftermarket leg, where the Feb-2026 and May-2026 calls describe mechanic loyalty programmes, BS4-to-BS6 and EV certification training, retailer demand generation and scholarships for mechanics' children; the dominant OEM business (~90% of India sales) is direct B2B where the OEM both chooses and pays.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: We have launched a mechanic loyalty program, conducting trainings with certifications on BS4 to BS6, electric vehicles and product equipment

TOLLROAD.rationale: Brakes, suspension, alloy wheels and castings are a material share of a two-wheeler's cost, and the calls show OEMs negotiating hard — raw-material inflation is recovered only with one- to two-quarter lags, the opposite of a customer who pays without negotiating; no certification-standard or regulatory anchoring gives Endurance toll-booth economics (ABS mandates benefit Bosch/Continental too).
TOLLROAD.quote: We recover such higher cost of aluminum from OEM customers both for direct and indirect impact

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a visible cost culture — backward integration into aluminium forgings, braided hoses, ABS valves and now in-house ECUs, plus the Chennai plant justified by lower freight and the FY27 capex bias to automation — but this is margin defence in a scale supplier, not a low-price-plus proposition; consolidated EBITDA margin has moved only from 11.5% (Q1FY23) to ~14.2% (FY26).
LOWPRICE.quote: started manufacturing both the stainless-steel braided hoses and the ABS valves in-house, which has helped us in lowering our cost

PRICING.rationale: Across all four years pricing is set by OEM contracts with lagged raw-material pass-through — Q1FY23 saw a 3.9% RMC hit the company could not fully recover, and management concedes EV pricing falls as volumes rise; better mix from premiumisation (IFF, ABS, assist-and-slip clutches) is product-mix improvement, not price increases above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: we have grown more than 130% with a customer where there is a quarter lag in getting the increases

BRAND.rationale: Endurance is a component supplier whose only consumer-facing brand asset is the acquired Italian aftermarket name Brenta plus a distributor-led aftermarket build-out; there is no heritage story, no sustained A&P spend and no premium pricing from brand — customers are OEM procurement departments.
BRAND.quote: They have a very renowned brand name called "Brenta" in the aftermarket and replacement business

INNOVATION.rationale: Named new products arrive every year with quantified order values — driveshafts (2022), single- and dual-channel ABS, inverted front forks, aluminium forgings, assist-and-slip clutches, solar dampers/actuators, and Maxwell's BMS, MCU and DC-DC converter — backed by a doubled brakes R&D facility commissioned Jan-2026; but R&D spend is never disclosed, gross margins are ordinary, and most technology is licensed or acquired (Adler, Gremica, BWI, KTM, Maxwell) rather than internally originated.
INNOVATION.quote: Our new integrated R&D facility for brakes was commissioned in January 2026 at Waluj

FORWARD.rationale: The strategic direction is explicitly backward, not forward — aluminium forgings, braided hoses, ABS valves and ECUs brought in-house — and the aftermarket goes to market through third-party distributors and retailers with no owned stores, franchising or D2C revenue disclosed.
FORWARD.quote: We are focusing on building long-term partnerships with distributors

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified share gain across the whole 2022–2026 record: order wins from every major OEM beyond Bajaj (TVS, Hero, HMSI, Suzuki, Royal Enfield, Kawasaki, Piaggio, Ather), cumulative non-Bajaj wins of ₹5,323 crores since FY22, ABS capacity going from 0.4m to 1.8m units against Bosch/Continental, Hero brakes business scaled to ₹200 crores with a line of sight to double, and EV sales compounding far ahead of the industry — all won on new platforms rather than by discounting, with margins holding.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Our CAGR growth in the last 4 years has been 71% as compared to EV 2-wheeler industry CAGR growth of 21%

CULTURE.rationale: Promoter-led with unusually stable leadership (Anurang Jain MD throughout, Massimo Venuti running Europe across all 16 calls), a consistently net-cash balance sheet, heavy organic capex (₹800 crores in FY26) and disclosure granular enough to track SOP promises; against that, the 13–14% margin ambition given in Aug-2022 was still unmet at 12.6% standalone in FY26 and dual-channel ABS slipped from "end of this calendar year" (2022) to June 2026, with no explicit owning of those misses on the calls.
CULTURE.quote: There was no consolidated net debt and the company had a net cash available of Rs. 6,128 million

MOATTEST.rationale: Real but rebuildable barriers: multi-year OEM validation and PPAP cycles, plants co-located with customers, four Greenfield sites and captive forging/ECU integration, plus acquired Italian know-how (Adler, Gremica, Frenotecnica) — yet the company itself is the challenger in ABS to entrenched Bosch and Continental, which shows a well-funded incumbent or entrant can and does hold these positions.
MOATTEST.quote: the competition is mainly from Bosch and Continental, which control the major market share in the Indian ABS 2W market

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 16 calls revenue is described as lumpy, project-execution-driven backlog with no licence/AMC/subscription stream, attach rates or renewal metrics; management repeatedly explains margin and revenue volatility as inherent to a project company rather than pointing to any annuity base.
RECURRING.quote: EIL is having revenue from the implementation of the project, where revenues are always fluctuating in nature because it depends on the execution of project

TOLLROAD.rationale: Consultancy fees are a small fraction of client project cost (fees ~INR100 crore on a INR2,500–3,000 crore bioethanol plant) yet are critical path, and management cites very few global players in niches like rock/salt caverns and sole-source awards for critical projects; but there is no certification/standards anchoring and most work is won by open tender.
TOLLROAD.quote: there are few players in the world who do rock caverns... we will be one of them

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is set by competitive PSU tendering with a stated ~20–25% hit rate and management explicitly declines to claim cost-plus terms; consultancy segment margin has been guided flat at 20–25% for four years with no price-increase or premiumisation language, and upside comes from change orders/provision reversals rather than price.
PRICING.quote: So it's a competitive market. So we'll not comment on that.

BRAND.rationale: Institutional reputation in hydrocarbon engineering wins nominated critical mandates (Euro-VI, refinery energy optimisation) and opened Dangote, Abu Dhabi and a five-plus-three-year Saudi Aramco agreement by FY26; but there is no consumer-style A&P, premium pricing or heritage-driven pricing benefit.
BRAND.quote: those were critical projects, that is how they came to us

INNOVATION.rationale: Repeated new-area development across the calls — green hydrogen, coal gasification, salt caverns via a technology alliance, the Chempolis bamboo-bioethanol partnership — but no R&D spend is ever disclosed and by Nov 2024 management admitted these had produced little beyond studies plus one ~INR300 crore biofuel job.
INNOVATION.quote: we have done a number of studies and kind of initial engineering assignments for that. And I think major implementation things have come as of now

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Trajectory shows genuine scale gain — order book from INR8,800 crore (Aug 2022) to a record INR15,109 crore (Mar 2026), inflow sustained ~INR8,000 crore two years running, with real international wins (Dangote expansion, Abu Dhabi record bookings, Saudi Aramco empanelment); but no explicit market-share figures or comparison versus named competitors is ever given.
SHAREGAIN.quote: This is the highest order book position in the history of EIL.

CULTURE.rationale: Stable long-tenured finance leadership, debt-free with ~INR1,200 crore cash, 100% dividend in FY26 and candid disclosure of provisions, JV shutdowns and the Middle East slowdown; offset by a persistent pattern of missed promises — INR3,200 crore turnover and INR350–360 crore PAT promised for FY23, a INR5,000 crore turnover 'by 2025' repeated in Nov 2024, versus INR3,849 crore actually delivered in FY26.
CULTURE.quote: we have corporate target of INR5,000 crores... within next 2, 3 years

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-replicate assets — decades of refinery/petrochemical process know-how, a rock-cavern track record with only a handful of global peers, and client empanelments/running agreements that take years to obtain — but the business is people-based consultancy won largely through open competitive bidding at a 20–25% hit rate, which a well-resourced rival can contest.
MOATTEST.quote: you have to empanel yourself with all the major clients there and you have running agreements with them

RECURRING.rationale: Both calls tie a service annuity to the installed fleet — services were 25.6% of FY25 revenue and 27% (~₹12bn) of H1FY26 revenue, with new service workshops (Raipur) and 4 service centres built near customers — but management never discusses attach rates, renewal rates, AMC contracts or customer advances/deferred revenue as a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: services are always related to the installed fleet and as the installed fleet grows from 5% to 10%, the service grows along

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct B2B to utilities, industrial customers and the parent group, won through competitive tenders/TBCB auctions; no prescriber, installer or trade-channel intermediary appears anywhere in either call.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: they have auctions on TBCB

TOLLROAD.rationale: The products — 765kV/500MVA transformers, steam turbines, HVDC and STATCOM systems, greenfield substations — are large lumpy capex items bid competitively, not a sub-1% consumable; management itself stresses order lumpiness and project-by-project tendering rather than certification or standards anchoring.
TOLLROAD.quote: the order development is not a uniform development... it's not unusual that you have fluctuations of the orders

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is no cost-obsession culture or itemised savings anywhere; the stated priority is the opposite — selectivity and margin over volume, with margins rising to 20.7% in H1FY26 on mix and operating leverage.
LOWPRICE.quote: We put value before volume. So, we are very much selective

PRICING.rationale: Margin expansion is real and sustained (12.7% FY23 → 15.7% FY24 → 19.3% FY25 → 20.7% H1FY26, ~18.9% adjusted) and management is explicitly value-selective, but they attribute the gains to operating leverage, export price arbitrage and mix — not to price increases taken without volume loss.
PRICING.quote: higher volumes have enabled us to benefit from economies of scale... increased export share has supported overall growth in margin through better price realizations

BRAND.rationale: Genuine B2B heritage — 100+ years in India, first turbo generators for Tata Iron in 1910, India's first HVDC line, plus customer and CII recognitions — but no consumer-style A&P, distributor leverage or premium-pricing evidence, and the brand itself is licensed from Siemens AG rather than owned.
BRAND.quote: Siemens Energy is a registered trademark licensed by Siemens AG

INNOVATION.rationale: 1,500 engineers, 4 R&D/engineering centres, membership of the global R&D network, an IIT Bombay MoU and named technology positions (PEM electrolyser leadership, SF6-free clean-air switchgear, waste-heat recovery) show a real innovation base, but no R&D spend is disclosed, no share of industry R&D, and core products are global with only local adaptation.
INNOVATION.quote: the products are global... our team comes in supporting and taking very high responsibility on the R&D

FORWARD.rationale: No own stores, franchising or D2C; the company is structurally constrained from reaching customers directly outside South Asia, with export access controlled entirely by the parent — the opposite of moving toward the end customer.
FORWARD.quote: we do not access all the markets out of South Asia by our own will. We have to do this as long as Siemens Energy asks us to do so

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Strong stated positions (30% of India's HVDC capacity, ~25% of the gas turbine fleet, leadership in grid stabilisation) and rapid growth — orders +49% FY25, backlog +22% to ₹184bn, exports +500bps — but share figures are levels not a rising series, and H1FY26 order intake actually fell from ₹72bn to ₹65bn with a 'muted' STATCOM market.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we had a growth in our backlog of 22%. And also, we had a book to bill of 1.5

CULTURE.rationale: Disclosure quality is good — one-offs are stripped out repeatedly (1.1%, 1.3%, 280bps, 260bps FX/commodity gains) to show underlying margins, and management answered pointed questions on weak ordering and STATCOM absence candidly — but with only ~11 months as a listed entity and two calls there is no track record of old promises delivered, and the capex announced (Kalwa doubling, Sambhajinagar, ₹20.6bn greenfield) is still unproven.
CULTURE.quote: Adjusting for these factors, our underlying operational profit margin improved from 17.2% to 18.9%

MOATTEST.rationale: Real barriers exist — a century-old installed fleet that feeds services, 30% of national HVDC capacity, eight capital-intensive factories and a ₹20.6bn greenfield transformer plant — but the technology, brand and export access all belong to the German parent rather than to SEIL, so the durable asset is partly a licence, not something the entity itself built.
MOATTEST.quote: we can access a very broad base of innovation, product development, new portfolio... we cooperate with headquarters in Germany

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 11 calls there is no license, AMC, subscription or renewal stream — revenue is pure product distribution, and the business consumes rather than is funded by working capital (59-67 net working capital days throughout FY24-FY26, with IPO proceeds and debt funding the cycle).
RECURRING.quote: our working capital days as on 31st March 2024 stood at 67 days

TOLLROAD.rationale: Distribution margin is a material, negotiated slice of the pharmacy's economics rather than a sub-1% critical input; there is no certification, standards or regulatory-anchoring language in any call, and management itself frames margin as coming from procurement bargaining and mix, not from customers who don't negotiate.
TOLLROAD.quote: Gross profit margins stood at 9.1%... improvement in gross margins was largely due to a change in product mix and procurement efficiencies

LOWPRICE.rationale: The model is textbook thin-margin/high-turn scale — ~10% gross, 4% EBITDA, ROCE lifted from 5.6% (FY24) to 14.6% (FY26) via operating leverage, procurement scale and working-capital optimisation — but the calls sell range and fill-rate convenience rather than a price advantage, and there is no itemised cost-culture disclosure.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are targeting to reach EBITDA margin of 5% plus, and that would be driven by both operating leverage as we continue to grow our scale

PRICING.rationale: In 11 calls management never cites a price increase; every margin gain is attributed to mix shift (MedTech/devices at 1.5-2x pharma gross margin), procurement efficiency and scale, and in FY27 guidance they are exiting low-margin business rather than repricing it.
PRICING.quote: there are certain low-margin business that we are giving up

BRAND.rationale: A B2B distributor with no heritage story, no A&P spend and no consumer brand; the one branded lever, private label, is explicitly still immaterial after eight years.
BRAND.quote: We have some private labels on home healthcare. But as of now, it's not scaled up. It's still pretty small

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent investment in a proprietary tech stack (Entero Direct B2B ordering, business-intelligence tools, technology-enabled last-mile) is described from the first call to the last as the differentiator, but no R&D spend is ever quantified and there are no named new products with revenue impact.
INNOVATION.quote: robust and technology-enabled last mile distribution infrastructure creates a very strong business moat

FORWARD.rationale: Entero moves backward toward manufacturers (exclusive pan-India distribution deals, marketing/promotion services), not forward to end consumers — no own stores, franchising or D2C is discussed in any call, and management explicitly expects retail pharmacy to stay fragmented and un-consolidated.
FORWARD.quote: less than 2% on store count front is consolidated into chains and we believe that in the near to long future, we don't see a massive consolidation happening on retail

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is quantified and persistent across the whole record: 20% vs IPM 9% (Q3FY24), 19% vs 7.6% (FY24), 26% vs industry 12% with 17.1% organic (Q3FY26), FY26 growth 1.6x IPM, reach up from 79,400 to 100,000+ pharmacies and 78 to 131 warehouses; local shares of 15-20% in Bangalore and double digits in Vizag/Cochin/Goa are named. The caveat is that roughly half the growth is bought inorganically (FY26: 15.6% organic, 16% inorganic).
SHAREGAIN.quote: we continue to grow faster than the industry, which grew by 12% and thereby increase our market share

CULTURE.rationale: Founders Agrawal and Sethi have run the company since 2018 and FY26 delivered all three stated guidance parameters (31.5% like-for-like growth, 4% EBITDA, ~₹96cr OCF) with candid quarter-4 math on the call; against that, the March-2024 promise of 5%+ EBITDA and 20%+ ROCE 'in the next two-three years' slipped (4% and 14.6% in FY26), the CFO turned over, and mistakes are rarely owned explicitly.
CULTURE.quote: I reiterate that we have delivered on all parameters of our guidance

MOATTEST.rationale: The concrete barrier is the eight-year, 42-acquisition pan-India footprint — 131 warehouses, 523 districts, 97,500 SKUs, 3,300 manufacturers with cold chain — which few can offer and which won them disproportionate GLP-1 share; but the underlying asset is aggregated local distributors that capital can also aggregate, and management concedes the target pool is huge with only 2-3 buyers, i.e. a well-funded copycat's main obstacle is time and money, not un-replicability.
MOATTEST.quote: the set of distributors available for acquisitions are huge, while the buyers are only 2 or 3

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 21 calls the revenue discussion is tube volumes, price/mix and pass-through contracts; there is no mention of licence fees, AMC/service revenue, attach rates, renewals or customer advances funding the business.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: EPL sells B2B directly to brand owners in a highly concentrated customer set — no prescriber, installer or trade professional stands between EPL and the paying customer, and no trade-training programmes are ever discussed.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: oral care is a very concentrated marketplace, right, there are only four players in the world

TOLLROAD.rationale: A tube is a small but critical input for FMCG customers, ~50% of revenue sits on contractual cost pass-through, and oral-care wallet wins are described as sticky long-term commitments; but the FY23–FY24 margin collapse and 'price corrections' show EPL does not price without negotiation like a true toll road.
TOLLROAD.quote: any oral care commitment, as you know, are long -term commitments... these are all wallet share gains, it will remain with us

LOWPRICE.rationale: The stated strategy is the opposite of low-price-plus: monthly price increases, premiumisation into Beauty & Cosmetics and sustainable tubes, and a march from ~15% to 20%+ EBITDA margins rather than passing savings to price.
LOWPRICE.quote: We are taking price increase every month

PRICING.rationale: EPL demonstrates cost-recovery pricing (monthly increases in FY23, landed-cost-plus-power pass-through in the FY26 Middle East crisis) but admits negative price/mix and 'price corrections' when commodities softened — pass-through, not pricing above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: have there been some price corrections in a few places with a few customers based on past or based on commodity softening of the past? Yes, there has been

BRAND.rationale: EPL is a contract packaging supplier — the brands, A&P spend and consumer heritage belong to its customers (Colgate-type oral majors, L'Oréal, P&G); no consumer brand equity, distributor leverage or adjacency launches under its own name are discussed.
BRAND.quote: the trusted partner for leading oral care and beauty and cosmetic brands globally

INNOVATION.rationale: Innovation is repeatedly named and monetised — Platina, Neo-seam tubes, sustainable tube mix rising 21%→29%→38% and directly credited with oral-care wallet-share gains, plus EcoVadis Platinum/SBTi firsts — but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, so the 'outsized R&D funded by gross margin' test is unproven.
INNOVATION.quote: Our sustainable tube mix reached 29% in Q1 FY '25 versus 21% in FY '24

FORWARD.rationale: No discussion of own stores, franchising, licensing or D2C anywhere in the excerpts; EPL remains a B2B manufacturer selling into brand owners.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Wallet-share gains are named repeatedly and by geography from FY25 onward (two new customers in Europe, India, Americas) on the back of sustainable-tube conversion, alongside new-market entry (Brazil FY23–25, Thailand in nine months) and the FY26 Indovida merger doubling revenue to ~$1bn — with share won on differentiation, not price.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have gained wallet with two more customers in Europe, which we never used to do earlier

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in 2022–24 calls were delivered — the 20%+ EBITDA margin target was hit and held for seven consecutive quarters, 500bps over 15 quarters, with debt cut to 0.52x — and management owns misses openly ('not pleased with the margin in Europe', 'B&C in AMESA... should have been better'); against that, leadership is unstable (three CFOs, two chairmen and a CEO transition inside five years) and ownership is PE/strategic rather than founder-led.
CULTURE.quote: B&C in AMESA, particularly in India, could have been better, maybe should have been better

MOATTEST.rationale: Real barriers exist — 21 plants in 11 countries co-located with customers, decades-long supplier partnerships, multi-year FMCG qualification and sustainability certification (only Indian packaging firm with EcoVadis Platinum) — but this is capital, not un-replicable scarcity, and the FY23 margin squeeze plus customer-driven price corrections show a well-funded rival could contest it.
MOATTEST.quote: strength of our decades-long supplier partnerships and meaningful scale allow us to be a reliable partner for our customers

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant fails on every leg: funding is expensive (cost of funds 7.13% in Q3 FY26 after SA rates of 6.08–6.18% and TD at 8.48%), operating costs are high and admittedly sticky (cost-to-income ~70–72% across FY25–FY26), and loan quality has been weak (credit cost 2.65–2.74% in FY25, PCR raised to 70% by one-time correction). Management describes itself as building a bank that pays 'relatively attractive rates of interest to depositors' — i.e. buying deposits, not sourcing them cheaply.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are progressing well on our long-term strategy of building a retail bank that offers relatively attractive rates of interest to depositors

PRICING.rationale: This is price deflation, not pricing power: NIM fell from a pre-crisis 8.5–9% to 7.29%, yield on gross advances declined to 15.63% (non-MFI 14.97%) on 'portfolio recalibration', and management concedes ~7–7.1% NIM is the 'new normal' with disbursement yields likely to fall further with market rates.
PRICING.quote: our NIMs are more or less bottomed out and somewhere around 7% to 7.1% is where we believe it should kind of stabilize

BRAND.rationale: There is no premium-pricing brand: deposits are gathered by paying above-market rates and by 'rate tweaking', and management explicitly frames moving away from rate-led acquisition as an ambition still ahead of them, while deposit growth stayed muted at 7–8% in FY26 even after Elite/ARTHA product launches.
BRAND.quote: we want to move from only rate-conscious approach to value proposition

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a steady, named product/technology cadence across the calls — new LOS for vehicle finance (2022), Selfie loan app with 1.5 lakh downloads and Microsoft Dynamics CRM (2024), credit cards, AD1/FCNR, gold loans, Elite/Elite Lite/ARTHA and Equitas 2.0 with ~6 lakh downloads (2026) — but this is product roll-out funded from thin margins, not high-gross-margin R&D dominance, and cost-to-income stayed at ~70%+ throughout.
INNOVATION.quote: Our Selfie Loan app for borrowers is seeing strong adoption with about 1.5 lakh downloads in the last quarter

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Advances growth has been respectable (22% Y-o-Y in Q4 FY26, record INR7,347 crore disbursement) with secured/used-vehicle/MSE lines compounding at 21–35%, but no explicit market-share figures are ever cited, microfinance share was deliberately cut from ~45–50% historically and 20% in Mar'24 to ~10%, and deposits — the harder share to win — grew only 7–8%.
SHAREGAIN.quote: total deposits grew 8% Y-on-Y to INR46,533 crores

CULTURE.rationale: Strong disclosure culture and stable leadership — Vasudevan has led all 16 calls since Jul 2022, routinely opens with 'what did not go well', pre-emptively took a one-time PCR correction to 70% and a INR180 crore floating provision, and flagged the labour-code hit transparently; but the delivery-versus-promise record is weak — the 25% FY25 loan growth guidance ended near 12–15%, the 2.25% ROA / high-teens ROE ambition stated in FY25 is still only 1.46% ROA in Q4 FY26, and credit-cost guidance was withdrawn mid-year in FY25.
CULTURE.quote: Now I'll talk about what did not go well in the quarter

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing in four years of calls articulates why a funded newcomer could not replicate this — the franchise rests on branch-gathered deposits priced above market, commoditised secured lending (used CV, used cars, LAP, gold), and bought-in technology, while microfinance economics proved cyclical enough to force the book from ~20% to 10% of advances.
MOATTEST.quote: anything up to 10% increase in diesel prices has no effect on the performance of the portfolio

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 15 calls there is no license, AMC, subscription or attach-rate stream — revenue is one-time branded-formulation sales through distributors, and the customer-funding test fails outright: FY26 receivables jumped from INR 458 crore to INR 680 crore and cash conversion collapsed, the opposite of a business funded by advances.
RECURRING.quote: OCF to EBITDA ratio came in at close to 50% for the financial year versus 105% for the last financial year.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The entire model is prescription-led: ~3,700 medical reps promoting to doctors, with management explicitly framing the sale as training the rep to promote in front of the HCP (Mar-23), and the FY26 Semaglutide win attributed to KOL credibility, cold-chain handling and patient hand-holding rather than end-customer marketing.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: it's not such a thick line when you do a promotion in front of a doctor. It's more about training and understanding the product

TOLLROAD.rationale: No certification, standards-body or 'tiny share of customer cost' language appears anywhere in the excerpts.

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine cost culture — YPM as the governing metric, in-sourcing derma and insulin manufacturing for 400-1,500 bps gross-margin gains, pruning low-margin tail brands — and the FY26 Semaglutide launch was deliberately priced below competitors, but Eris runs 80%+ gross margins and 37% EBITDA, not the low-margin/high-turns model.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our products are priced lower than competition. We believe that these are more sustainable price points in the long term.

PRICING.rationale: Price increases are called out as a FY26 Q4 growth driver and gross margins held ~80-86% for years, but the record also shows deflationary exposure — FDC bans on Glimisave MV and Zayo's LOE collapse, insulin market value shrinking on innovator exit, and Sundae launched below competitor pricing with guided lower initial gross margin.
PRICING.quote: In Q4 we will see the impact of price increases accruing to the fullest extent.

BRAND.rationale: Eris is a branded-formulations house with real brand equity — five brands above INR 100 crore, six of nine acquired Dr. Reddy's brands holding top-3/top-5 positions, 80%+ gross margins — but the brands are largely bought (Oaknet, Glenmark, Dr. Reddy's, Biocon) rather than heritage-built, and there is no sustained A&P or provenance narrative.
BRAND.quote: Today, we have five brands with more than Rs. 100 crores of revenue.

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur each year with revenue impact (Dapagliflozin combinations, Esaxerenone developed in-house and first-approved in India, Aspart/Degludec pipeline, Sundae), but R&D spend is never disclosed or benchmarked against the industry — capital goes to acquisitions and fill-finish capex rather than research.
INNOVATION.quote: We were the first company to develop this in India, put it through clinical trials, and get it approved by the drug controller.

FORWARD.rationale: The calls are silent on own stores, franchising, royalties or D2C economics; the only customer-ward move mentioned is a patient-care support platform, which is not quantified as a channel.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified share gain across the whole 2023-2026 arc: IPM rank 29 at IPO to top-20 by FY25, derma #3 with 7% covered-market share after the 2022-23 deals and 14.2% vs 8.6% market growth in FY26, and RHI cartridge share from 8% at acquisition to 24-26%, with Sundae ranked #1 by volume in month one.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have tripled its market share in less than 2 years since, which is the highest ever gain seen in the Insulin segment by any player

CULTURE.rationale: Management discloses bad news plainly — a dedicated hits-and-misses slide quantifying INR 55-60 crore of abandoned launches, two straight years of ~INR 50 crore insulin sale loss from Bhopal delays, falling OCF and stretched debtor days — and delivered promised Oaknet margin uplift and the 2x net-debt/EBITDA deleveraging; against that, growth has been acquisition- and leverage-led (net debt peaked above INR 2,700 crore) and several guided launches slipped.
CULTURE.quote: Looking back at the key hits and misses during the year, the key misses were largely threefold

MOATTEST.rationale: There are articulable barriers — an approved insulin fill-finish site management says saved two years versus greenfield, cold-chain and endocrinologist relationships that let Sundae take #1 volume share in month one — but the core branded portfolio is largely purchased assets in molecules open to generic entry, as the FDC bans, Zayo LOE and crowded Semaglutide field show.
MOATTEST.quote: an approved fill-finish site is the most critical component of the last mile in building competitive advantage for a scalable and profitable GLP play

RECURRING.rationale: Aftermarket spares and service is a disclosed, growing revenue vertical — one of four verticals created post-merger, running at 17-21% of agri-machinery revenue, and 12-16% of railway revenue in Aug 2023 — but across all 11 calls management never discusses attach rates, renewal rates, AMC contracts, or customer advances/deferred revenue as a funding source.
RECURRING.quote: Service and spare part business, catering to a wide range of agri machinery products... we expect the growth should be significant in the coming years, and we'll see very large potential across all 3 verticals, especially on the parts part and the engine part

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The evidence is silent on any expert intermediary who specifies the product while another party pays; the farmer both chooses and buys, and dealers are distribution points rather than prescribers.

TOLLROAD.rationale: A tractor is the farmer's largest capital outlay, not a sub-1% consumable, and the calls repeatedly show demand swinging on GST rates, state subsidies, monsoon and finance availability — the opposite of a price-insensitive toll.
TOLLROAD.quote: post the introduction of the GST -the revised GST slab rates, we've seen a shift in the segment wherein the customer is actually moving towards a slightly higher horsepower tractor

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine, repeated cost programme — material and fixed-cost rationalisation from Aug 2023 through Feb 2026, merger synergies of '10%, 11% top line', and localisation of imported content to lift merged-entity margins — and Kubota explicitly uses EKL as a frugal global sourcing base, but this is margin repair rather than a scale-driven low-price-plus model.
LOWPRICE.quote: With EKL well-established large vendor base and Frugal cost structure along with Skilled workforce Kubota is looking at India as a key sourcing base

PRICING.rationale: Across the trajectory pricing is reactive, not powerful: price rises are small and commodity-triggered, the CE price increase of Jan 2025 met customer resistance and took two quarters to stick, and by Feb 2026 management said tractor pricing would wait on competitor moves.
PRICING.quote: It will also depend on how the competition actually responds to that. So, based on that, we will take a call. So, if there is a requirement and the industry also passes on the prices, then we will also take the similar move.

BRAND.rationale: Real brand assets — 80 years of heritage, three distinct brands (Farmtrac, Powertrac, Kubota) and ~1,500 exclusive dealers — but the record shows brand strength failing the market-share test in the North/Central core and no evidence of premium pricing or A&P leverage.
BRAND.quote: we celebrated 80 years of spreading prosperity and impacting lives

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur every year — Worldmaxx (FY25), PROMAXX (Jan 2025, order inflow now exceeding supply), Kubota KA6/KA8 transplanters and U22-6 mini-excavator, Hydra-72 crane (Q3 FY26) — but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, and management concedes product gaps and 'limited availability of key models' cost them share.
INNOVATION.quote: The Promaxx series continue to gain traction with the order inflow now exceeding current supply level and we are scaling up our production to meet this demand.

FORWARD.rationale: Moves toward the customer are real but modest: an exclusive-dealer network expanded from 1,240 (Q1 FY24) to ~1,500 (Q2 FY25), a captive NBFC (Escorts Kubota Finance) registered with RBI in FY25, and 'strengthening financial partnership' cited in Feb 2026 — but no own-store economics, franchise royalties or D2C share are discussed.
FORWARD.quote: We obtained the certificate of registration from RBI for Escorts Kubota Finance Limited (EKFL), and we are gearing up to begin operations for captive finance of EKL products

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gains are episodic rather than persistent: +41bps to 9.7% in Q1 FY24 and mini-excavator share +151bps to 18.5% in Q2 FY26, but tractor share slipped from 11.8% (Q2 FY25) to 11.28% (Q2 FY26) and Q3 FY26 domestic volume grew 12% against a 23.2% industry — management's own framing was arresting decline, not gaining.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Overall, the market share has not grown, but the continuous decline has been able -- we have been able to arrest that in quarter 2.

CULTURE.rationale: Management discloses bad news promptly and specifically — flagging the 1.5-2% merger margin dilution in advance and owning it, admitting the Powertrac series slipped a quarter, disclosing the Rajasthan land withdrawal over water assurances, and reporting the RDSO hold on INR382 crores of railway orders — and stays net-debt-free while investing in a greenfield plant; against that, the FY27-28 greenfield timeline and mid-teens margin promise are still undelivered and Chairman/MD titles have rotated repeatedly since FY2021.
CULTURE.quote: Rajasthan government was not able to give us the assurance for the water supplies were to withdraw the expression of interest on Rajasthan

MOATTEST.rationale: No articulable barrier survives the test — the calls show a company that must follow competitor pricing, has lost tractor share to rivals in its core geographies, and whose main structural asset (Kubota parentage and its global network) is a partnership rather than something a funded entrant could not assemble; the greenfield plant that would deepen the advantage is still years away.
MOATTEST.quote: our domestic performance was moderated by regional disparity. The North and Central markets continued to underperform

RECURRING.rationale: Zomato Gold is a paid subscription that management says covers ~50-55% of food-delivery GOV (Aug 2024 call), and it demonstrably reduces customer delivery charges — but there is no discussion of attach rates, renewals, deferred revenue or customer advances as a funding source, and the core business is transactional commission/take-rate revenue, not licence or AMC streams.
RECURRING.quote: almost half of our GOV is from Gold members... we are ballpark in the same 50-55% zone today on the Zomato Gold membership base

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: No evidence in any of the excerpts of a professional/prescriber channel choosing the product on the end customer's behalf; restaurants and local store partners are supply, not recommenders, and demand is driven by direct consumer acquisition spend.

TOLLROAD.rationale: The commission/take rate is a large, actively negotiated share of a restaurant's economics rather than a sub-1% critical input — management describes 'driving parity on take rates' with low-take-rate restaurants (Aug 2022), and in Blinkit sellers pass cost benefits through to stay competitive; there is no certification, standards or regulatory anchoring language anywhere.
TOLLROAD.quote: we are not actually increasing the top end of the take rates for restaurants but rather essentially normalizing take rate at restaurants which could be at lower take rates right now

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management explicitly rejects discount-led price competition as a trap and instead frames price reduction as a scale dividend funded by improving unit economics and higher capex-per-store efficiency (Jul 2026), plus cost discipline on fixed costs (Aug 2022) — but there is no itemised cost-culture disclosure or no-frills positioning, and margins are being built up rather than deliberately kept thin.
LOWPRICE.quote: prices can come off with scale, but then that's a choice that we make to pass on the benefits of scale to customers rather than trying to compete on price with someone else

PRICING.rationale: In food delivery they have raised platform fees consistently while MTUs and order growth accelerated (May 2026, Jul 2026) and take rates have risen since Aug 2022 without volume loss; but Blinkit shows the opposite — flat-to-falling NAOV, price matching forced by competitors, and management saying they do not expect NAOV to grow.
PRICING.quote: increase the overall revenue per order by increasing the platform fee and then channel that revenue to select cohort of customers

BRAND.rationale: The Zomato app's traffic is used deliberately to launch new brands (Blinkit, District) at low customer-acquisition cost, and by Q4FY26 competitors' pullback let them acquire at 'extremely low cost' — evidence of brand-driven distribution leverage and adjacency stretch, but no heritage story, no premium pricing from brand, and A&P is acquisition spend rather than brand building.
BRAND.quote: we're seeing extremely low cost of customer acquisition and we, therefore, continue to see value in keeping marketing spends high

INNOVATION.rationale: A steady cadence of named new businesses with real revenue impact — Blinkit pivot (2022), Gold, District (2024), Bistro (2026) — and category/assortment expansion cited as a core growth block; but there is no R&D disclosure, no share-of-industry-R&D framing, and gross margins are thin rather than innovation-funded.
INNOVATION.quote: we're planning to launch this as a separate app and brand. We want to take the advantage of the traffic that we have on the Zomato app

FORWARD.rationale: Eternal owns the customer-facing layer end to end — 3,000 owned-capex dark stores guided by Mar 2026, Hyperpure warehousing, and Bistro's own kitchens (~10 added per quarter) — and explicitly takes the store capex itself rather than letting partners fund it; the franchise-royalty/third-party-funded-growth element of the pattern is absent by choice.
FORWARD.quote: even when we open stores with partners, our policy now is that we actually take the upfront cost of the capex because we find that we are able to do a higher quality capex

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, disclosed share gain across the four years: food delivery GOV compounding ~30% FY20-FY24 and still ~20% in FY26, Blinkit going from number three or four in southern markets to leading player by NOV, share taken from modern retail and e-commerce, with 60% NOV CAGR guided to FY29 — and management repeatedly refuses to buy share with subsidies.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Now, we are the leading player by NOV in most of these markets and we strongly feel that discount-led growth is not sustainable

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on early calls were delivered — the Aug 2022 Zomato adjusted-EBITDA breakeven target and the cut in the Blinkit investment budget from $400m to $320m, then the 3,000-store guidance reaffirmed in May 2026 ('we remain firmly on track'); management owns failures publicly (the southern-market discounting approach that 'didn't work'), declines to give metrics it cannot defend, and refuses growth it deems unhealthy.
CULTURE.quote: our initial approach in those markets was like typical e-commerce thinking... That didn't work for us initially in some markets in the south

MOATTEST.rationale: The articulable barrier is physical: a dense owned dark-store and warehousing network on constrained urban real estate, built over years, which management argues discounting cannot replicate because shelf space is finite — but the counter-evidence is loud, with several well-capitalised rivals in the same market and Q1FY27 described as the peak of competitive intensity, so replication is expensive rather than impossible.
MOATTEST.quote: In quick commerce, you're working off smaller store sizes, so you have limited shelf space... the constraint is the store size

RECURRING.rationale: After-sales servicing is repeatedly named as a strategic pillar (Aug 2022 'watch servicing and after sales service an extremely high standard'; Nov 2024 pan-India servicing cited as a differentiator; May 2025 'the aftersales service business is also growing', driving the UAE service/talent subsidiary), but across 11 calls management never quantifies attach rates, service revenue share, renewals or deferred revenue — and working capital runs heavily negative-of-the-good-kind's opposite (inventory 154→177 days, funded by IPO/QIP equity, not customer advances).
RECURRING.quote: the aftersales service business is also growing

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Evidence points the other way: Ethos sells direct to end customers through its own boutiques and website, with a 'large database of HNI customers', in-house luxury watch consultants, concierge service and 250k Instagram followers — there is no prescriber or trade intermediary choosing the product on the buyer's behalf.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: a highly specialized team of luxury watch consultants, targeted content, watch insurance and dedicated after sales service

TOLLROAD.rationale: The product is a discretionary big-ticket purchase (ASP rose from Rs 84,000 to Rs 2.16 lakh), not a sub-1% critical input to a customer's cost base; the only 'certification' language is the Certified Pre-Owned resale vertical, which is a retail format, not an industry standard.
TOLLROAD.quote: Our ASP for H1 FY25 stood at Rs. 2,15,952

LOWPRICE.rationale: The strategy is the explicit opposite of low price — management repeatedly describes exiting cheaper segments and trading up ('we are continuing to get out of lower price points and into brands at a higher price point', Nov 2023), with share of luxury/high-luxury at an all-time high and a new above-Rs 20 lakh Haute Horology format in May 2025.
LOWPRICE.quote: we are continuing to get out of lower price points and into brands at a higher price point

PRICING.rationale: Realised prices rise steadily (ASP +7.4% in FY25 alongside 15.5% volume growth; discounting 'steady reduction' since Q1FY23) and management treats luxury demand as inelastic on the GST question, but pricing is set by the Swiss brands' MRP, not by Ethos — Nov 2024 shows India priced below global and price moves dictated by CHF/INR and GST, so this is mix-led premiumisation more than owned pricing power.
PRICING.quote: the elasticity and inelasticity of luxury products is well known

BRAND.rationale: Ethos has retailer-level trust and scale advantages — authorised-dealer status, marketing muscle, pan-India servicing, and successful stretch into adjacent categories under the same name (Rimowa luggage, Messika jewellery, Second Movement CPO) — but the heritage and provenance story belongs to the Swiss principals, not to Ethos, and no sustained A&P spend or share-plus-premium data is disclosed.
BRAND.quote: our customers come to us because we are authorized

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a regular cadence of named new formats and verticals with revenue attached (Second Movement CPO Rs 32cr H1FY24 → Rs 43cr H1FY25 → +30%; Rimowa ~Rs 20-24cr billing; Messika Chanakya Mall; the 22,000 sq ft City of Time and the new Ethos Haute Horology concept in May 2025), but this is retail-format innovation — no R&D spend is disclosed or claimed at any point in the 11 calls.
INNOVATION.quote: Ethos Haute Horology, which is our newest concept, which works on... prices above INR 20 lakhs

FORWARD.rationale: Ethos already occupies the retail end rather than integrating forward, but it shows the same mechanics — 50→73 boutiques with 100+ targeted in FY26, roughly a third of Q1FY23 billings through digital, home/office delivery, mono-brand boutiques — and the group integrated backwards by acquiring the Favre Leuba brand and taking exclusive Indian and UAE retail rights to it.
FORWARD.quote: nearly one-third of our business is now coming through digital medium

SHAREGAIN.rationale: The trajectory shows real gain — revenue Rs 174cr Q1FY23 to Rs 1,252cr FY25, same-store growth of 15.5% in H1FY25, exclusive brands from 24% pre-COVID to ~31%, brand count 35→60+, and 'Ethos has become the preferred partner for many international brands' — but when asked directly for market share in Nov 2024 management answered 'I have no factual data on this', so no explicit share series exists.
SHAREGAIN.quote: I have no factual data on this

CULTURE.rationale: Promoter-family led with Yashovardhan Saboo as chairman throughout and son Pranav progressing CFO→CEO→MD, conservative debt (Rs 60cr to Rs 6.9cr), and candid disclosure of bad news — the Rs 4.65cr FY25 forex loss, the GRAP IV pollution shutdown, hedging 50% of exposure after the CHF hit; against that, the FY25 target of '20-plus boutiques' delivered 14, the IPO store plan was revised mid-stream (75→145-150 stores) with a QIP raised while Rs 90cr of IPO money was still unutilised, and three CFOs cycled through in three years.
CULTURE.quote: At the beginning of the year, we set a target to open 20-plus boutiques... Several boutique openings were delayed

MOATTEST.rationale: There is a concrete, repeatedly articulated barrier — exclusive retail agreements with 60+ Swiss brands (Ulysse Nardin, Jacob & Co., Tudor, Favre Leuba) built over decades, plus allocation-constrained supply, described in Aug 2022 as taking 'many years to develop and difficult to replicate' — but these are contractual, revocable, and a well-funded Indian conglomerate could court the same brands, so it falls short of a time- or capital-based barrier that money cannot bridge.
MOATTEST.quote: Relationships with luxury brands and their owners typically take many years to develop and are difficult to replicate

RECURRING.rationale: The model is product-upfront plus an AMC annuity on an 8mn+ installed base, with bookings billed in advance sitting as unamortized revenue on the balance sheet; AMC bookings grew double digits for four straight quarters into FY26 and management deliberately shifted mix to multi-year contracts to lock in lifetime value, alongside a new filters-aftermarket push.
RECURRING.quote: if you look at the liability that we carry on our balance sheet, which is towards the unamortized revenue , that continues to remain very, very healthy

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: The FY26 filters strategy explicitly courts independent 'market service technicians' and distributors who choose which filter goes into the customer's purifier, with engagement programmes and genuine-part education — but the core product business is sold through advertising, e-commerce, retail and direct sales to end consumers, not via prescribers.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: an engagement program for market service technicians and for the distributors

TOLLROAD.rationale: This is a discretionary consumer purchase, not a small-but-critical input to a business customer: management works constantly on affordability barriers (INR6,499 entry UV product, buyback schemes, discounts) and calls out demand slowdowns — the opposite of customers paying without negotiating; BIS is the only standards anchor mentioned.
TOLLROAD.quote: our solution that’s affordably priced starting at INR6,499 for a UV product

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine institutionalised cost culture — the COGS programme, leakage control in service charges, digital AMCs cutting service cost, opex down 27bps as a share of revenue — but this funds A&SP and margin expansion rather than a low-price/high-turn scale model; gross margins run 58–60%.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our COGS program is now well institutionalized and is helping create the headroom for growth investments.

PRICING.rationale: Realisation gains have come from premiumisation and mix (premium innovations, the INR79,999 Arctic Blaze) rather than list-price increases — in Q2FY25 management stated flatly that they took no pricing — and the only broad 6–7% increase (April 2026) was cost-driven catch-up on input inflation, with margin headwinds still flagged for FY27.
PRICING.quote: in neither of the categories, was there a pricing led growth . We did not take pricing

BRAND.rationale: Aquaguard is presented as a 40-year heritage power brand carrying sustained and rising A&SP (up 40% in Q2FY25, 23% in Q3FY26, 13.2% for FY26) and is being stretched into adjacencies — air purifiers (2.7x in FY26), water softeners, robotics — while gaining share in water purifiers.
BRAND.quote: We are pioneers in the cleaning and water categories in India with a 40 years plus heritage. In Aquaguard, we have a power brand that enjoys tremendous consumer trust

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur every year with clear revenue impact (Superio/Blaze/Eden in FY23, under-the-counter and instant-hot in FY25, Arctic Blaze in FY26) and premium innovation demonstrably lifted ASPs, but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified and there is no claim to a share of industry R&D.
INNOVATION.quote: our premium innovation, one of them was under -the-counter product, another was the instant hot water product , both of these helped strengthen our ASPs

FORWARD.rationale: The stated strategy is to become a 'D2C health and hygiene leader' with a direct sales force, owned nationwide service network and online-to-offline D2C programmes on the installed base, but no own-store count, franchise royalties or D2C revenue share is ever quantified, and growth is increasingly coming through e-commerce and modern trade third parties.
FORWARD.quote: transforming into a vibrant D2C health and hygiene leader

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gains are claimed repeatedly — retail share up in both traditional and modern trade in Q2FY25, water purifier share up sequentially and year-on-year in Q3FY26 — but never quantified with actual share numbers, and management concedes two new aggressive entrants in the category.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Our Water Purifiers performed ahead of the category, leading to market share gain both sequentially and year-on-year.

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made on the first call in 2023 were delivered: margins went from 6.3% in FY23 to 12.2% in FY26 with three consecutive years of expansion, net debt of INR193cr became net cash of INR443cr, and FCF/PAT stayed above 100%; management also owned the Q3FY26 miss openly rather than explaining it away, though leadership below the MD/CFO pair has churned.
CULTURE.quote: With the benefit of hindsight, it is now clear that the Q3 sell-out growth was not in line with our earlier projections and the post-festive slowdown was not anticipated.

MOATTEST.rationale: The nationwide service network, 8mn+ customer installed base and 40-year Aquaguard brand are assets a funded entrant could not assemble quickly, and the multi-year AMC mix is explicitly used to 'elbow out' grey-market rivals — but the products themselves are copyable, e-commerce entrants are already pressing, and the filters aftermarket is openly contested by unbranded operators.
MOATTEST.quote: the more multi-year mix that you do, the more is your chance to kind of elbow out the gray market operators

RECURRING.rationale: Across all nine calls there is no discussion of AMC/service contracts, attach rates, renewals, subscriptions or deferred revenue as a funding source; the only adjacent metric is warranty cost, which is an expense, not a recurring revenue stream.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Management talks about distributors, channel networks and go-to-market reach, but never about mechanics/installers as prescribers, trade training programmes, or professional-driven specification. The evidence is silent on the middleman mechanic rather than contradicting it.

TOLLROAD.rationale: No certification/standards or 'tiny share of customer cost' language appears; the closest is Railways' mandated battery-change cadence, which is a customer policy driving tenders, not a toll-road economic. Insufficient evidence either way.

LOWPRICE.rationale: A genuine and repeatedly itemised cost culture runs through the record — fixed expenses cut from 20.2% to 19.4% of sales (Nov 2022), 'cost excellence projects' worth 175bps of gross margin (Feb 2026), and factory/employee/warranty cost control offsetting a 90bps gross-margin fall (May 2026) — but Exide positions on premium products and brand, not low price with high asset turns.
LOWPRICE.quote: we could offset the drop in gross margin through our internal controls

PRICING.rationale: Exide does raise prices (three tranches Jan–Mar FY26 plus ~3% on 1 April, ~5-6% cumulative) without losing volume — Q4 FY26 was its highest-ever revenue quarter — but this is cost-recovery with a lag, not pricing above inflation: management admits price rises trail raw-material moves, that it deliberately forwent a Q3 hike, and that gross margin still fell from 31.6% to 30.1%.
PRICING.quote: we have taken increases which maybe amounts to about, let's say, about 5% to 6%

BRAND.rationale: Brand and distribution are the recurring, management-asserted core of the franchise from the 2022 call ('75 years… deep customer connect') to the Feb 2026 and May 2026 calls, backed by 100% supply positions on new Tata Sierra and Kia Seltos SKUs and adjacency launches (AGM, Ultra/PowerBox, solar grid-tie) under the same name.
BRAND.quote: Exide, with its advanced product portfolio, pan-India distribution network, and a strong brand recall, will continue to benefit from growth opportunities

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur each year — AGM batteries for premium PVs, Ultra/PowerBox inverter ranges, 'front access' data-centre batteries, premium export SKUs homologated for US/Europe — but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified, and the flagship lithium bet relies on licensed SVOLT technology rather than in-house dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: we have very good technology support from SVOLT

FORWARD.rationale: No own-store counts, franchise royalties, D2C revenue share or e-commerce logistics investment are discussed in any of the nine calls; distribution is described only at the distributor/dealer-network level.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Management claimed broad share gains in Nov 2022 and cites lithium telecom-pack share in Nov 2024, but no explicit share percentages are tracked over time, and the later record shows share loss in structurally shifting segments — telecom fell from ~10% to ~3% of sales and exports from 8% to 5%.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Exide has been gaining share rapidly in the market, not only against unorganized players, but also against organized players

CULTURE.rationale: Positives: candid, granular disclosure of bad quarters (Q2 FY26 'washout', antimony at 6x, GST pass-through absorbed), a zero debt:equity balance sheet in 2022, and follow-through on the 'One-Exide' reorganisation promised in FY25 and reported delivered in FY26. Against that, the flagship promise has slipped badly — SOP guided for 2024 in Nov 2022, 'no change in our originally published schedule' for 2025 in Nov 2024, yet by May 2026 only customer samples are shipping on ~Rs. 4,802 crores invested — and chairman/CFO turnover has been heavy.
CULTURE.quote: we should be seeing SOP in 2025. So, no change in our originally published schedule

MOATTEST.rationale: The lead-acid side has a concrete replication barrier — a 75-year brand with pan-India distribution and OEM homologation that a funded entrant could not rebuild quickly — but the lithium cell business, built on licensed technology, imported Chinese raw materials and government incentives, explicitly targets mere parity with imported landed cost, which is not a durable barrier.
MOATTEST.quote: our target will be meeting the landed cost of the imported cell

RECURRING.rationale: Federal has a genuinely annuity-like, granular retail liability base (deposits >90% retail, CASA crossing ₹1 lakh crore) that funds the bank in advance, plus a fast-compounding fee/cross-sell stream (fee income +24% YoY in Q4FY26, wealth management launched), but management never discusses attach rates, renewals or an installed base in the product-plus-service sense — the recurring stream is ordinary banking float, not a post-sale contract.
RECURRING.quote: Our fee income trajectory during the year has been extremely encouraging, reflecting improved cross-sell, better product penetration and a more diversified revenue profile.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: A meaningful share of new customers arrives through third-party fintech partners and co-lending rather than direct marketing (Jan-2024 call: partnership-led account opening running at 4,000–5,000 accounts/day after filtering), but these partners are volume aggregators competing on economics, not trusted professionals whose recommendation removes price sensitivity — and management's main commentary is about cutting waste and fraud in that channel.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: We started this partnership -led new account opening about 2, 2.5 years back. We have learned a lot in terms of -- so that we can cut wastage between us and our partners.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Banking credit and deposits are the customer's primary cost, not a sub-1% critical input, and the calls describe an environment of aggressive rate competition where customers switch on price — the opposite of a toll road; there is no certification, standards or oligopoly language anywhere across the 17 calls.
TOLLROAD.quote: in a market where we have seen intense and sometimes irrational rate competition

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant is partly visible — CASA ratio up 271bps YoY to 32.94% with cost of deposits down to 5.43%, wholesale deposits deliberately shrunk, and high-quality loans (GNPA 1.62%, NNPA 0.37%, credit cost 47bps, both decade bests) — but the cost culture is not elite: cost-to-income is still 52.86% and NIM only 3.20%, so this is a good-credit franchise improving its funding, not a structurally low-cost operator.
LOWPRICE.quote: Our CASA ratio improved to 32. 94%, an increase of 87 bps Q -o-Q and 271 basis points Y -o-Y. This is amongst one of the best in the industry.

PRICING.rationale: Federal is explicitly a price-taker: term deposits described as 'very price elastic' in 2022, repo-linked loans reprice T+1 with 125bps of cuts flowing straight through, and management says it cannot price out of the market; NIM fell over the period and was defended by mix, not by raising prices.
PRICING.quote: You cannot play price out of the market with our risk appetite. We are not inclined to grow by flexing our risks.

BRAND.rationale: There is real heritage and one genuinely differentiated franchise — a 90-year legacy and NRI/NRE deposits crossing ₹1 lakh crore with rising market share (7–7.5% of India's NR deposits back in 2022) — but the Feb-2025 strategy required a brand refresh with a celebrity ambassador and a new visual identity in FY26, which is evidence the national brand was not yet doing the work of winning share or price.
BRAND.quote: Pride in a 90 -year legacy while actively shaping the next chapter

INNOVATION.rationale: New business lines have been launched repeatedly and did scale (credit cards, personal loans, microfinance, CV/CE, gold, business banking from 2022; wealth management in FY26), and management cites technology/AI and fintech partnerships — but there is no R&D disclosure, no share-of-industry-innovation claim, and gross margins (NIM 3.2%) do not fund outsized innovation spend.
INNOVATION.quote: our influence of technology, use of AI our structural changes that we are putting in place

FORWARD.rationale: The bank owns its distribution and is investing in it — 65 branches in H1FY24, 39 in Q4FY26 guided by a 'scientific and data-driven' network study, a branch operating-model redesign and a new in-house wealth business — but a bank branch network is native distribution rather than a manufacturer integrating forward, and a chunk of sourcing runs the other way through partners.
FORWARD.quote: During the quarter, we also launched our wealth management business.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is real but selective and not persistent across the board: incremental credit share ~2% vs 1.2% stock share in 2022 and NR deposit share still rising in FY26 with CASA growth of ~21% YoY described as among the best in industry — yet in FY26 both headline loan and deposit growth ran below system, a deliberate mix trade-off management defends rather than denies.
SHAREGAIN.quote: Given the balance sheet realignment that you were doing this year, both your loan and deposit growth has been below system in FY'26.

CULTURE.rationale: Disclosure quality and conservatism are consistently good — bad news flagged early (AIF exposure, wage/pension catch-up, MFI credit costs), a voluntary ₹456 crore buffer from a one-off gain ahead of ECL, PCR held ~75%, credit cost beating guidance, and small promises kept (no Saturday calls) — but the multi-year delivery record is mixed: the 1.4% ROA promised for FY24 was met, while the 1.5% ROA promised for 'the next 12, 18 months' in Jan-2024 was not, with ROA falling to 1.00% in Q1FY26 and only recovering to 1.24% by Q4FY26 under a new MD.
CULTURE.quote: We will work towards it over the next 12, 18 months.

MOATTEST.rationale: One asset would genuinely be hard for a funded newcomer to rebuild — the Kerala/Gulf NRI remittance and NRE deposit franchise, ~₹1.03 lakh crore and gaining share, built over decades of branch and diaspora relationships and explicitly called 'our moat'; the rest of the book (corporate, LAP, gold, MFI, fintech-sourced retail) is contested on price and reproducible, and management concedes the arbitrage in capability is closing.
MOATTEST.quote: Our NRE deposit, which is our moat, reached a significant milestone crossing the INR 1 lakh crore mark

RECURRING.rationale: This is a balance-sheet lender, not a product-plus-service model: growth consumes capital rather than being funded by customer advances, and every call discusses capital adequacy, leverage (4.0 → 4.6 → 4.89) and the need for direct assignment/co-lending to release capital. No attach rates, renewals or deferred revenue anywhere across the 12 calls.
RECURRING.quote: A 40% growth in AUM depletes capital adequacy and has resulted in a leverage increasing to 4.6

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Management explicitly exited its intermediary-sourced business because it did not earn its cost of capital, and has pushed toward own-branch and doorstep origination instead; there is no professional-channel or trade-training model.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: It was a DSA run business. It was not fitting with our strategy.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Fedfina is a high-yield lender (15.7-17.5% yields, gold at 19%+) funded at ~8.7%, and management itself concedes a poor cost record; the FY26-27 cost improvement is a repair story, not an entrenched low-cost culture, and the bank-variant test fails since it has no deposit franchise.
LOWPRICE.quote: We have admittedly had a history of stubborn Opex.

PRICING.rationale: Yields are market-set and drifting down, not raised: FY26 yields fell 12 bps YoY and gold origination yields were shaded in Q4 to chase disbursals, with management conceding competitive pressure is coming.
PRICING.quote: Our yields reduced 12 bps year-on-year due to a never before growth in the gold loan book

INNOVATION.rationale: There is repeated, credited product/process innovation — doorstep gold loans scaled from nil to ~INR1,787 Cr (96.5% YoY) and 15%+ of gold AUM, Salesforce/BRE-driven underwriting, and co-located 'Vyapar' branches — but no R&D disclosure, no industry-R&D share, and none of it produces pricing power.
INNOVATION.quote: Our doorstep gold loan initiative has paid off really well.

FORWARD.rationale: The company owns its distribution and keeps deepening it — 750+ branches, 148 new gold branches in FY26, 70 ST LAP branches folded into gold branches, and doorstep delivery direct to the customer — while deliberately exiting third-party DSA-sourced lending; but this is normal NBFC branch banking, not a manufacturer capturing downstream margin.
FORWARD.quote: we have opened 34 new gold branches this quarter, bringing our total to 148 new branches this year

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Gold AUM grew 76% YoY to INR10,352 Cr with 12% tonnage growth (i.e. real volume, not just gold price) and secured AUM +41%, alongside improving credit cost (1.8% FY25 → 0.8% FY26) and ROA 2.6% — but no explicit market-share figures, and the FY25 episode shows earlier growth in ST LAP and unsecured BL was bought with underwriting quality and had to be unwound.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the secured book has grown a little under INR5,800 crores this year, a growth of approximately 41% year-on-year

CULTURE.rationale: Under Parvez Mulla the calls follow a disciplined promise-then-scorecard format — 12 priorities listed at the start of FY26 and each reported against — with candid admission of the ST LAP delinquency 'injury', the DSA-income crutch and stubborn opex, and delivery on the credit-cost guidance (guided ~1%, delivered 0.8%); offset by heavy discontinuity, with the entire FY24 board and MD exiting and True North fully selling out in Q1 FY27.
CULTURE.quote: These were our promises at the start of the year. And against that, our year as well as quarter has performed as follows

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing described would stop a funded entrant: gold lending against standard collateral in leased branches, replicable underwriting, and management itself acknowledges competition is simply yet to arrive in its pockets rather than being barred from them.
MOATTEST.quote: The competition pressure that you are talking about is yet to play out

RECURRING.rationale: There is a genuine installed-base annuity in the replacement/aftermarket lamp business that grows as the vehicle parc ages (INR141 crores in FY24), but across all 15 calls there are no licence fees, subscriptions, AMCs, attach/renewal rates or customer advances — and working capital is a use of cash (receivables rose in FY26 after stopping bill discounting).
RECURRING.quote: during the current year, we registered a good growth in the replacement market. It's INR141 crores

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Fiem sells direct to OEM engineering/purchase teams via RFQs, with OEMs deliberately multi-sourcing and shifting models between suppliers; there is no professional/installer channel, no trade training programme, and no low-price-sensitivity dynamic anywhere in the 2022–2026 calls.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Every customer is looking for multiple sources and we have taken the businesses from other competitors and some of the business has gone to other company.

TOLLROAD.rationale: Lighting is a small share of vehicle cost and is critical, but the calls repeatedly show the opposite of toll-road economics: prices are back-to-back cost pass-throughs both ways, models are re-tendered, and share moves between Fiem and Lumax/others; no certification, standards or oligopoly anchoring is claimed.
TOLLROAD.quote: these are passed on this price escalations, any increase or decrease, both ways is passed on to the customer

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a real cost/efficiency culture — integrated manufacturing, factory efficiency drives, ~3x asset turns on capex, and itemised energy savings (65% solar at Hosur plus 20% wind) lifting EBITDA margin from 11.6% (Q1FY23) to a record 14.67% (Q4FY26) — but Fiem does not compete on a low-price, no-frills proposition to win share.
LOWPRICE.quote: At our Hosur facility, around 65% of our energy needs are already met through solar power with a further 20% being added through wind energy.

PRICING.rationale: Management states explicitly and repeatedly (FY24 and FY26 calls) that realisations are set by back-to-back compensation with OEMs, with commodity and FX moves passed through in both directions and a lag; margin gains come from mix, LED penetration and operating leverage, not from independent price increases.
PRICING.quote: we have a back-to-back path to compensation from customers and it continues in a similar manner

BRAND.rationale: Fiem is a B2B Tier-1 supplier: across four years of calls there is no A&P spend, no heritage/consumer-brand story and no brand premium — management notes lighting defines the OEM's brand identity, not Fiem's.
BRAND.quote: Lighting and electronics are emerging as the key element in defining brand identity.

INNOVATION.rationale: Consistent, named technology pipeline across the years — 80+ development projects (FY23), laser headlamp, night vision, ambient lighting, ADB and matrix lighting, plus an in-house EMC/EMI lab commissioned in Gurgaon (FY26) — and LED share rose 39% (FY20) to 63% (FY26) with a 100% LED pipeline; but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified as a share of sales or industry, and innovation is largely customer-funded co-development.
INNOVATION.quote: we are working on three main technologies. One is a laser technology... we propose to be the first in the industry to launch that.

FORWARD.rationale: Every call describes a pure OEM-supply and replacement-channel model; there are no own stores, no franchising, no D2C or e-commerce initiatives across FY23–FY26, and the only 'move toward the customer' is winning more OEM platforms.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Genuine expansion of the customer set (20+ EV OEMs, Hero, Harley, Norton, Mahindra 4-wheeler, Mercedes approval) and revenue up from INR1,834cr FY23 to INR2,791cr FY26, but core wallet share is contested — Yamaha tail lamps fell 82% to 64% and TVS 77% to 69%, wallet-share disclosure was discontinued in FY24, and in FY26 Lumax grew 50%+ at HMSI versus Fiem's 16%.
SHAREGAIN.quote: that wallet share actually we tried to work out... this time, we are not able to do that

CULTURE.rationale: Long-tenured family leadership (J.K. Jain, Rahul Jain, Rajesh Sharma present on every call since 2022), net-zero-debt balance sheet with INR276cr cash, rising dividends, and delivery against promises (12–15% FY25 guidance, 14%+ EBITDA target, capex programme all met); offset by openly-flagged but repeatedly-slipping promises — Gogoro hub motors never produced revenue, 4-wheeler 'meaningful contribution' promised since FY24 is still only INR100–150cr guided for FY27 — and reduced disclosure on wallet share and margin escalations.
CULTURE.quote: We continue to be a net zero debt company.

MOATTEST.rationale: Real time-based barriers exist — multi-year OEM qualification (five Mercedes plant visits before global small-lamp approval, 18–24 month development cycles), model-life design-in and tooling — but the calls also show well-funded incumbents (Lumax and others) winning models away, so the barrier slows entrants rather than making the position un-replicable.
MOATTEST.quote: This was their fifth visit to our plant... their process development time is around 18 months to 2 years with Mercedes.

RECURRING.rationale: Across all nine calls the discussion is entirely one-time product sales of wire, cable and fibre; no licence, AMC, subscription, attach-rate, renewal or deferred-revenue disclosure appears anywhere.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales run exclusively through a trade channel (730 distributors, ~4,500 channel partners, 2,000 active) rather than direct to end customers, but across the calls there is no evidence of electrician/contractor training programmes, prescriber loyalty or professional switching costs — and the Jun 2026 call shows the channel behaving as a price-sensitive stockist, not a loyal recommender.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we do not sell directly to any project, we sell it through our distribution channel only

TOLLROAD.rationale: Wire is a tiny share of the cost of building a house, yet the Jun 2026 call shows exactly the opposite of toll-road behaviour — retail demand fell when prices rose, and management itself warns demand can turn inelastic-in-reverse; no certification, standards or 'don't switch' language.
TOLLROAD.quote: The retail one where you go to the hardware market... that has taken a hit

LOWPRICE.rationale: Beyond a working-capital consultant project (inventory cut from 1.8 to 1.5 months in Feb 2024, 69 to 61 days by Feb 2026) there is no discussion of a cost culture, itemised savings, no-frills positioning or passing savings to price; the evidence is silent on the pattern itself.
