BRAND.quote: Renault Duster has also been launched with our Ranger HP e tyre, demonstrating a long -standing faith of customers in our offerings

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur every year across the calls — UX Green (80% sustainable materials), Levitas Ultra, XF/XM fuel-efficient TBR series, Embedded Smart Tyres, four new OTR tyres, Shresth Plus — with patent filings and premiumisation tied to 16-inch-plus tyres, but R&D spend is never quantified, share of industry R&D is never claimed, and gross margins (12-13% EBITDA) are not the high-margin engine the pattern requires.
INNOVATION.quote: JK Tyre ha d introduced Embedded Smart Tyres for passenger cars to deliver real -time data on tyre operating conditions

FORWARD.rationale: A consistent multi-year push toward the customer: the Leh Steel Wheels flagship centre (Aug 2023), ~200 dealers plus 35 pit stops and 25+ fleets added in Q3FY26, 50+ new brand shops in FY26, plus rural distribution expansion and direct mass-merchandiser supply at Tornel — but own-store share of sales, franchise royalties and D2C revenue are never quantified.
FORWARD.quote: adding nearly 200 dealer s pan India ... and 35 pit stops for enhancing customer services

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volume growth turned strong by FY26 (domestic +16% in Q3, +21% in Q4; TBR replacement +19%, OE +53%) and Tornel claims the highest share in Mexican mass merchandise, but explicit domestic share numbers are never given and an analyst pointed out CEAT grew ~25% against JK's 15%, which management explained away rather than rebutted with share data.
SHAREGAIN.quote: one of our competitors CEAT, they almost reported like a 25% growth on a similar base ... and we reported around 15 %

CULTURE.rationale: The record shows promises kept over the three years: the Rs.1,100 crore TBR/PCR capex announced in Aug 2023 was commissioned, deleveraging delivered (net debt/equity 1.16x in Q1FY24 to 0.71-0.73x by FY26), the Cavendish turnaround and merger were completed as flagged, disclosure was improved when analysts asked, and the leadership team (Singhania, Bajoria, Kinra, Aggarwal) is long-tenured — though the calls are consistently promotional, mistakes are rarely owned, and Rs.6,110 crore of debt-funded expansion is being taken on.
CULTURE.quote: capacity utilization was scaled up from around 30% to over 95%, ma king it JK Tyre 's yet another successful turnaround acquisition

MOATTEST.rationale: Nothing in the calls articulates why a funded entrant could not catch up — capacity is buyable (JK itself is adding Rs.6,110 crore of brownfield lines), protection from Chinese imports comes from regulation and anti-dumping duty rather than any company asset, and the Mexican business is described as exposed to peso moves, tariffs and Asian import influx.
MOATTEST.quote: there is export to the rest of the world from China and the competitiveness from China to India. But, there is a regulation in p lace for Chinese imports.

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 11 calls revenue is described as episodic, per-encounter hospital care with no licence, subscription, AMC or renewal stream; growth is funded by capex and internal accruals, not customer prepayments, and no deferred revenue or attach-rate metric is ever discussed.
RECURRING.quote: if you look at it is a collection of each individual encounters between a doctor and a patient

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Doctors are the de-facto referrers and insurers pay ~55% of revenue, and management's site-selection logic is explicitly about attracting affiliated consultants with better infrastructure — but there is no trade-training programme or channel-investment language, and insurers negotiate rates hard (biennial rate revisions).
MIDDLEMAN.quote: it becomes a natural choice for a lot of these skilled medical practitioners to want to affiliate and associate with us, and it becomes a win-win symbiotic kind of association

TOLLROAD.rationale: Nothing toll-road-like: the service is a large, negotiated cost to the payer, with insurance contracts repriced on a rolling basis every one to two years rather than customers paying without negotiating; no certification-standard or magic-ingredient economics anywhere in the calls.
TOLLROAD.quote: we have had a couple of renewals from the insurance company, which happened once in 2 years, so, some price increase that has kicked in

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is genuine capital-cost discipline — Dombivli delivered 500 beds in ~24 months at INR425 crores with no escalation, Indore beds at ~INR30 lakh/bed, and the whole model is built around the insured population to solve affordability — but no consumer-facing low-price positioning, no itemised opex savings culture, and margins are mid-20s rather than thin-margin/high-turn.
LOWPRICE.quote: we built 750,000 square feet... all in just over 24 months. And we did it without any cost escalations on time, on budget, no surprises

PRICING.rationale: Prices do rise without volume loss (high-single-digit Pune insurance revision in FY24, ARPOB from ~Rs 53,000 in H1FY24 to Rs 67,700 in FY26), but management repeatedly caps the mature-asset lever at inflation and says ARPOB is a byproduct it does not even target — this is inflation pass-through plus case-mix maturation, not pricing power above cost inflation.
PRICING.quote: in Thane, there is just one lever that is an inflation-linked price hike

BRAND.rationale: A trust-and-heritage story is consistently invoked — 16-plus years in Thane in the 2023 call, 'over the last 2 decades' by 2026, and BKC framed as earning patient trust — but there is no A&P spend disclosure, no premium-pricing-plus-share evidence, and management denies any special strategy against new entrants.
BRAND.quote: the kind of health care to the region around Dombivli that the community has come to expect from Jupiter over the last 2 decades

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Expansion from ~1,000 to ~3,000 beds with a stated ambition to lead Western India, and Indore/Pune occupancy ramps are real, but no explicit market-share numbers are ever given, mature-asset growth is inflation-only, and Q3FY26 top line slowed to single digits — capacity-led growth rather than demonstrated share capture.
SHAREGAIN.quote: cement our position as the leading hospital group, in Western India

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in early calls were delivered later — debt-free post-IPO in Nov 2023, the 2,500-bed target built out via Dombivli/Pune South/Mira Road, Indore beds added a quarter early, and Dombivli commissioned ahead of the guided Q1FY27 on budget; management refuses quarterly guidance, flags bad news promptly (the INR6.4 crore Labour Code hit, the coming EBITDA drag and depreciation load), and self-imposes a 3x EBITDA debt ceiling under stable founder leadership.
CULTURE.quote: We had set ourselves a target of commissioning it by Q1 FY27, and I'm very pleased that we beat that and opened ahead of schedule

MOATTEST.rationale: Owned land in finite dense micro-markets (a 2-acre Mira Road plot, the MMRDA-allotted BKC site, ~INR1.5 crore/bed of owned infrastructure) plus multi-year build and accreditation/empanelment cycles are real time-and-capital barriers, but management itself argues a well-funded entrant next door is unproblematic because demand is unmet — which is an argument for a growing market, not for un-replicable advantage.
MOATTEST.quote: neither us nor them will have to have any extraordinary strategies... the community has a lot of unmet need

RECURRING.rationale: Management explicitly tracks a recurring-revenue stream in wealth/asset management — recurring AUM up 33% Y-o-Y to ~INR33,100 crores with recurring at 29% of total AUM (Feb 2026), and states the focus 'will always be on recurring revenues' — but there is no product-upfront sale, attach rate, renewal rate or customer-advance funding dynamic; revenue remains heavily transactional and deal-driven.
RECURRING.quote: The recurring AUM of all our wealth businesses grew by 33% year-on-year to INR33,100 crores. The proportion of recurring to total AUM has increased to 29%.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: A large share of distribution runs through intermediaries who select products for end investors — 7,400+ active independent financial advisers/distributors (Nov 2022), 874-922 franchisees and 1,000+ RMs by FY26 — and management talks of 'rebuilding all our relationships with several key distributors', but there is no evidence of professional training programmes or expert-driven price insensitivity.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we have 7,400+ active independent financial advisers/distributors

TOLLROAD.rationale: The calls contain no discussion of a small-share-of-customer-cost critical input, certification/standards positioning, or regulatory anchoring; the evidence is silent on this pattern.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The trajectory is the opposite of a cost culture: FY25–FY26 calls repeatedly flag margin compression from deliberate spending — 'increase in investments both in talent as well as infrastructure' — with wealth operating PAT falling to INR19 crores from INR30 crores and the AMC loss widening; no itemised savings or no-frills positioning anywhere.
LOWPRICE.quote: Performance for the quarter in Wealth and Asset Management in terms of profitability is impacted, again, by increase in investments both in talent as well as infrastructure

PRICING.rationale: Pricing evidence points to deflation, not power: wholesale mortgage yields fell from north of 15% to 13.5–14% ('almost 100 to 125 basis points reduction in yield', Nov 2022), broking yields fell on the F&O mix shift, and IPO/deal execution is gated by what 'valuations investors are willing to take for issuers' rather than by JM's own pricing.
PRICING.quote: our yields, which used to be north of 15% and our incremental yield for new loans... is growing at around 13.5% to 14%

BRAND.rationale: Management leans on the JM Financial name as an asset it intends to stretch into wealth and asset management, and the franchise carries multi-decade client relationships ('they've been there for more than almost 2 decades'), but there is no A&P spend, no premium pricing evidence, and the brand was demonstrably damaged by the March 2024 SEBI order that cost them equity deals.
BRAND.quote: Our brand, JM Financial, deserves to be much larger in these businesses. And we will just continue to invest.

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a regular cadence of named new products with disclosed impact — two AIF approvals (real estate fund and pre-IPO fund) in Feb 2026, a credit fund in Jun 2026, equity MF basket expansion, plus disclosed digital/technology investment — but no R&D disclosure, no share-of-industry-innovation claim, and these are distribution products rather than a self-funding innovation engine.
INNOVATION.quote: We've got approval for two alternative funds, real estate fund as well as pre-IPO fund

FORWARD.rationale: The group has steadily built owned and franchised customer touchpoints — 682 franchisee locations in 197 cities (Nov 2022) rising to 874–922 franchisees and 72–73 branches plus 135–151 affordable-housing branches by FY26 — and pushes direct customers onto its own broking platform, but franchise royalties and D2C revenue share are never quantified.
FORWARD.quote: branches have increased by 11 to 73 branches and franchisees have increased by 27 to 922

SHAREGAIN.rationale: There are explicit share claims — #1 in QIP deals in CY2024, #2 among Indian banks in M&A/PE advisory, 15–20% capital-market share, MF AUM up 3x — but share is stable rather than persistently rising, it was dented by the SEBI order ('we may have lost out on some large deals'), and the lending book was deliberately shrunk from ~INR10,000 crores to ~INR4,000 crores.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our market share in any given year will be anywhere 15% to 20% on the capital market side

CULTURE.rationale: The 2024 pivot was delivered against stated guidance — INR270 crores of recoveries against INR250–300 crores guided, PCR taken to 93–100% upfront and deliberately early ('it's just good to clean it up'), borrowings cut from INR16,145 to INR12,143 crores, dividend raised as promised — and bad news (SEBI order, NPA spike, wealth margin drag) is disclosed on calls; against that sits the March 2024 regulatory action itself and heavy MD-level churn in the management record.
CULTURE.quote: We had guided INR250 crores to INR300 crores of recovery in each of the years FY26, '27 and '28, we've achieved over INR270 crores in FY26

MOATTEST.rationale: The most defensible asset is a multi-decade IB franchise and client relationships that a newcomer cannot buy quickly ('I've never seen it in my career over the last 3 decades'), but management's own account shows the advantage is people-based and mobile — they hired 'top-quality talent' from disrupted competitors and added 80-odd RMs in a year — which is exactly what a well-funded copycat could rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: we've actually used this opportunity to go and get some top-quality talent

RECURRING.rationale: Not a product-plus-service model, but the bank explicitly builds an 'anchor bank' installed base — 3.6→3.8→3.9-4.0 active products per affordable-housing/micro-LAP customer, with penetration rising on a growing base (gold 1.6%→2.2%→3.0%) — and long-dated mortgage contracts plus customer deposits fund the book.
RECURRING.quote: every property-related relationship on a contractual basis is at least about 10 to 15 years

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sourcing through intermediaries (BC partners, DSAs) is being deliberately reduced rather than cultivated — the BC book fell to 5% of the MFI book and Micro LAP growth was sacrificed in Q1 FY27 to shift toward direct sourcing.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: We have been slowly trying to amend the model more towards direct sourcing. It causes a blip in the quarter.

LOWPRICE.rationale: The bank variant requires cheap deposits and low operating cost; JSFB runs cost of funds of 7.4-8.0% with cost-to-income that worsened to 61.3% in FY25 against a stated 54% ambition, and it competes on underserved-segment yields, not price.
LOWPRICE.quote: our bias was to take 57% down in the three year period to a 54% number. We have unfortunately this year have gone the wrong way; we have become 61.3%

PRICING.rationale: Management repeatedly reports no yield erosion across products through the MFI stress and a post-shakeout 'advantage period' with unmet demand, but NIM gains come from falling cost of funds and lower interest-in-suspense rather than price increases above inflation.
PRICING.quote: we haven't seen any customer pricing drop in any of our products

BRAND.rationale: There is a 16-year, 12-million-customer franchise, a consistent 'Jama Karo, Jana Karo' positioning and a Business Times/KPMG 'best Small Finance Bank' award (Feb 2026), but no A&P spend, premium pricing or heritage-led share gain is evidenced.
BRAND.quote: these customers know the brand. They know the bank

INNOVATION.rationale: A steady cadence of named new products with disclosed size — two-wheeler and gold graduating to scale (gold +237% FY25, +140% FY26), used car and supply chain next, Credit Line on UPI and loans against shares in FY27 — plus proprietary secured-lending scorecards and AI projects; but no R&D spend or industry-share-of-R&D disclosure.
INNOVATION.quote: gold and two wheelers have become that businesses... we have now started focusing to put our measured investment money into used car growth and supply chain financing

FORWARD.rationale: Distribution is owned and being optimised — 781 outlets in 2024 growing to 822 branches by FY26 with 42 relocations to better spots, 98%+ digital account opening — and Micro LAP is being moved from DSA to direct sourcing, but this is ordinary bank distribution rather than franchising or D2C economics.
FORWARD.quote: existing branches relocated to better spots to help liability growth as well as affordable housing, that's 42

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent above-industry growth is cited across years (FY25 advances 19% vs industry 11%, deposits 29% vs 11%; FY26 both 23%) and share is being taken in MFI as competitors retreat, with credit standards tightened not loosened (Rs.50,000 exposure cut-off, 77-80% under guarantee programs) — but no explicit market-share percentages are given.
SHAREGAIN.quote: our branches haven't changed. Our number of people in sales haven't changed in unsecured. Yet we've seen such a strong growth

CULTURE.rationale: Guidance given in Q3 FY26 was met item-by-item in Q4 (PAT, credit cost, SMA), the 2024 promise to keep growing secured at ~40% was delivered through the MFI stress, bad news is owned plainly (cost-to-income miss, the promoter holdco rating downgrade addressed head-on), and leadership has been stable (Kanwal, Sandur, Raman) with capital adequacy rising to 20.7% without a raise.
CULTURE.quote: Last quarter, we had given specific guidance what to expect this quarter... I'm very happy to report that we have met all the guidance's

MOATTEST.rationale: Management names the multi-product anchor relationship as the moat, backed by a 16-year, 12-million-customer base, 822 branches across 25 states and a proprietary secured-lending scorecard — but nothing here is beyond a well-funded competitor with an SFB licence to rebuild in a few years, and the bank itself concedes rivals will return to MFI.
MOATTEST.quote: This is our important slide... this is why we do think that the bank has a competitive moat

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 16 calls revenue is discussed purely as tonnes shipped at prices that reset with raw material, with guidance framed as EBITDA per ton (Aug 2022 through May 2026); no licence, AMC, subscription, attach-rate, renewal or deferred-revenue stream is ever mentioned.
RECURRING.quote: the prices are governed by the movement in the raw material prices

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: JSL sells through fabricators, pipe & tube makers and retailers and invests in them via the Jindal Saathi co-branding scheme (5th year by FY25, ~35 partners), Saathi Pragati authenticity/loyalty programmes, and 155-hour fabrication courses embedded in four government ITIs (Jan 2026) — but the intermediaries are converters buying on price, not prescribers insulating JSL from price competition.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: in co-branding like we have around 35 partners working with us on this co-branding scheme

TOLLROAD.rationale: Stainless steel is the dominant input cost for its customers, not a sub-1% critical ingredient; customers switch freely to cheaper Chinese/Indonesian imports, which hold ~30-50% share across the period, and JSL must lobby for QCOs and anti-dumping duty rather than rely on standards lock-in.
TOLLROAD.quote: subsidized inferior materials continue to enter our country

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly cites cost competitiveness, scale and backward/forward integration (JUSL, Chromeni, Indonesia SMS to 4.2mt) as how share is retained against imports, and CRAP mix rose from 60% to 70% of HRAP:CRAP by Q3FY26 — but there is no itemised cost-savings culture or no-frills discipline described on the calls.
LOWPRICE.quote: Jindal Stainless retains its market share through its agility, cost competitiveness

PRICING.rationale: Realisations are an explicit pass-through of nickel/ferrochrome, with blended ASP falling ~4-4.5% in Q3FY26, and in May 2026 management conceded it could not pass on a sharp fuel/ammonia cost spike because importers' costs had not risen — the opposite of pricing power.
PRICING.quote: everything we are not able to pass on to our customers because our competitors, importers

BRAND.rationale: Brand-building is real but recent and B2B-rooted: Jindal Saathi co-branding since ~FY20, QR/Saathi Seal anti-counterfeit programme, and only in FY26 a first-ever brand ambassador (Ranveer Singh), the Jindal Infinity campaign and an SRH cricket tie-up; no evidence yet of premium pricing or share won on brand.
BRAND.quote: The onboarding of Ranveer Singh as the company's first -ever brand ambassador

INNOVATION.rationale: There is a steady drip of new grades and application wins — Jindal Durasafe for foot-over-bridges and the Srinagar rail tunnel (2022), RRTS train sets, ICF Chennai acceptance for Kolkata metro side walls (Jan 2026), defence grades (May 2026) — but no R&D spend, pipeline quantification or share-of-industry-R&D is ever disclosed.
INNOVATION.quote: our stainless steel has been accepted by ICF Chennai for the fabrication of external side walls

FORWARD.rationale: A consistent multi-year move toward the customer: Jindal Stainless Steelways service centres selling direct to OEMs, downstream acquisitions (JUSL, Chromeni, Rathi), CRAP capacity heading to 2.67mt by FY28, and in May 2026 a first fabrication plant at Patalganga — but this is downstream processing, not owned retail, franchising or D2C.
FORWARD.quote: positioning beyond material supply to value -added fabrication

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Volumes compounded (highest-ever quarterly sales in Q1FY25, +11% in Q3FY26, FY26 deliveries 2.57mt, +8%) with a 3.5mt FY29 target, and margins were protected rather than bought — in 2022 they deliberately took a 5-10% volume cut rather than chase share — but management describes 'retaining' share against 30%+ imports and exports shrinking to 8%, not sustained gain versus named rivals.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we don't want to drop our margins , because what will happen then is, we have to significantly drop our margins to get that extra market share

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in early calls were delivered later: the INR18,000-20,000/ton guidance first given in Aug 2022 was held and beaten (21,300 average in 9MFY26), the JSL-JSHL merger, JUSL and Chromeni acquisitions and Indonesia SMS all completed (the latter ahead of schedule), while net debt/EBITDA fell to 0.55x and net debt/equity to 0.15 with dividends initiated — under a stable family-led team (Abhyuday Jindal MD throughout FY21-FY26).
CULTURE.quote: the focus for us is that to maintain a very strong prudent balance sheet and financial ratios

MOATTEST.rationale: The advantage is integrated capacity and scale that Chinese and Indonesian mills demonstrably already replicate and undercut — imports have run at 30-50% share for the whole period, and management's defence rests on the government granting QCOs and anti-dumping duty rather than on anything a funded entrant could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: the share of imports rising to nearly 50%

RECURRING.rationale: The FY26 call describes a genuine post-sale annuity — discharged IPD patients continue on a medicine regimen, and the May-2024 call mentions selling patients a one-year package — while customer advances are explicitly a funding source (Q4 FY26: advance bookings held, INR8 crore of advances carried into June, and pre-GT practice of booking advances as revenue). But there are no attach rates, renewal rates or deferred-revenue disclosures, and the Swadeshi Health Card loyalty scheme is still in trial.
RECURRING.quote: Every patient who recovers and leaves our hospital takes a medicine regimen that provides recurring product revenue for months or years.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Demand is intermediated by doctors — management deliberately shifted business from cash-on-delivery to clinic visits because the prescribing doctor lifts repeat rates from 30% to 60-65%, and ~600 doctors plus 750 wellness experts sit on the company payroll supplying medicines exclusively. But the intermediary is an employee, not an independent professional whose reputation the company must court, and there is no trade-training programme; end payers are increasingly insurers.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: when a patient comes to the clinic and meets the doctor. So his trust is of a different kind... his repeat ratio is 60%, 65%

TOLLROAD.rationale: The offering is the customer's whole healthcare bill, not a sub-1% critical input, and demand is manufactured through TV, newspaper and social-media campaigns rather than being non-negotiable. NABH is an accreditation the company receives, not a standard it sets or sells.
TOLLROAD.quote: On ABP News, at least 15 times a day, I have started a new slot

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a real structural cost advantage — INR3-4 lakh capex per bed versus INR50 lakh-1 crore for allopathy, break-even at 35% occupancy, payback under 6 months — and the Jun-2026 call itemises cost ratios falling (manpower 21%→19%, ad 12%→8%, other opex 15%→9%, total 70%→56%). But this is a high-margin model (89% gross, 44% EBITDA), not the low-margin/high-turns variant, and savings are retained rather than passed to price.
LOWPRICE.quote: our capex per bed is approximately INR3 lakhs, whereas, against that we spend INR50 lakhs to INR1 crore on allopathy hospitals

PRICING.rationale: Average revenue per occupied bed has been essentially flat for three years (INR7,900 FY24 → 8,280 Q1FY26 → 8,337 Q3FY26) and management says so explicitly; all earnings growth has come from occupancy, volume and cost leverage, plus 10% free treatment for the poor. Hoped-for realisation gains depend on insurer and Ayushman tariffs (INR8,800-9,400), i.e. third-party rate cards, not the company's own pricing power.
PRICING.quote: We did not increase this. But the occupancy has increased.

BRAND.rationale: Trust and word-of-mouth are the stated acquisition engine, sustained A&P across ABP/Zee/print has been backed by growing volumes (IPD +65%, OPD +69% in FY26), and the name is being stretched into OTC, supplements, beauty, diagnostics, a Swadeshi Health Card and UAE/Nepal/Kazakhstan. But the brand is barely five years old at scale, leans heavily on the founder ('Acharya ji') persona, and the borrowed heritage is Ayurveda's rather than the company's.
BRAND.quote: Satisfied patients and the common man are our marketing channel, word of mouth, completely free.

INNOVATION.rationale: 85-89% gross margins do fund a visible pipeline — clinical trials, 180 published papers by Feb-2026, 330+ SKUs, and named launches with disclosed revenue impact (Pet Yakrit Pleeha Shuddhi Kit crossing INR10 crore/month, NutriRoz next, 16 products targeted in 2026). But no R&D spend is disclosed in rupees or as a share of sales, the research-output claims (550 papers written in one year) are unaudited, and the Entero distribution tie-up stalled, so innovation-led dominance is asserted more than demonstrated.
INNOVATION.quote: My target was that when the first product crosses INR10 crores in monthly sales, I will launch the second product.

FORWARD.rationale: Across all four calls the company moves steadily toward owning the customer relationship: 117 owned facilities against only 35 clinic franchises (franchise count deliberately shrunk over three years), doctors on payroll, exclusive medicine supply into its own network, D2C e-commerce, and now OTC pharmacy retail plus own diagnostics — capturing both clinical quality and product margin.
FORWARD.quote: Out of our 117 facilities, only 35 are clinic franchises. All other doctors are on our payroll, and the control remains with our organization. We supply medicines exclusively

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Growth has compounded well ahead of any market (FY24 INR324cr → FY26 INR801cr, IPD admissions 5,700 in FY23 to 40,450 in FY26) with an accreditation-share claim (49 NABH facilities, ~10% of India's NABH-accredited base) and international expansion with local adaptation (Marathi/Gujarati packaging, UAE/Nepal/Kazakhstan). But there are no share numbers versus named competitors, and management frames itself as 0.1% of the market with 'no competition' rather than tracking share.
SHAREGAIN.quote: out of all the NABH accredited centres in India, 10% share is with us

CULTURE.rationale: Several old promises were kept — 2,850 beds by FY26 delivered, main-board migration completed Aug-2025, Big-4 audit (Grant Thornton) engaged — with zero debt, capital-light expansion and an unusually candid Q4 FY26 walk-through of INR21 crore of one-time provisions. Against that: segment margins were refused as 'not handy', a 2024 NABH accreditation count was challenged by an analyst against the public register, guidance questions are deflected ('I don't pay attention to numbers'), and revenue was previously booked on unbilled advances until the new auditor stopped it.
CULTURE.quote: previously when we closed the financial year quarter, we used to book our advances as well. But GT said... you should only book the patient once the bill is generated

MOATTEST.rationale: The economics that make the model attractive — INR3-4 lakh per bed, third-party manufacturing, leased or college-tied hospitals, demand bought on TV and social media — are precisely what a funded entrant could replicate in a few years; management's defence is an assertion of uniqueness rather than a concrete barrier, and the durable assets (NABH accreditations, papers, founder persona) are not capital- or time-locked at a level a rival could not match.
MOATTEST.quote: we do not see anyone working like us... Ayurveda is a totally blue machine market. We do not have any competition.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: GGBS is sold through RMC producers and specified via approved concrete mix designs, and the company runs concrete testing labs, mix-design advisory and 'continuous customer education' plus a 13,000+ dealer network (1,000 new dealers in the North, 25% exclusive) — but the RMC producer is the paying customer, not a disinterested prescriber, and it switches on cost.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: Concrete testing labs offering concrete mix design, testing and investigation services; Techno-commercial team to advise customers about optimal GGBS usage

TOLLROAD.rationale: Cementitious material is 42-45% of RMC raw-material cost, not a tiny sliver, and the May 2026 call states customers explicitly re-compare OPC-GGBS vs OPC-fly-ash economics and switch mixes — the opposite of 'don't negotiate, don't switch'; BIS/regulatory certification is the only tollroad-like trait.
TOLLROAD.quote: they will look at a design mix and compare the cost between OPC GGBS and OPC fly ash

LOWPRICE.rationale: Cost obsession is itemised and tracked across all three calls — a INR400/ton savings programme (>50% delivered by FY26, guided to ~75% in FY27, broken into INR69-70 power, INR36 logistics, INR4 premiumisation), industry-lowest clinker factor of 51%, lead distance cut to 273km, and slag/co-location synergies with JSW Steel; but returns are still constrained by 2.9x net debt/EBITDA and sub-scale grinding utilisation (62% in Q1 FY26).
LOWPRICE.quote: we have taken a target of reducing our cost under various cost heads by almost INR400 over the next year and a half to 2 years

PRICING.rationale: GGBS realisation has been flat-to-down for years (INR3,761 FY24 → INR3,773 FY25 → INR3,684 9M FY26) with management consciously refusing price increases to buy penetration, and cement realisation fell 3.9% QoQ in Q3 FY26 — this is a price-taker in a commodity, with earnings improvement coming from volume and cost, not price.
PRICING.quote: we have consciously not increased the prices despite the cement prices having gone up... we want to drive adoption or penetration of GGBS

BRAND.rationale: There is JSW group lineage and 'Customer Loyalty + Trust' positioning, an A-category brand launch in the North backed by TV/print/hoarding spend, and 57% premium share within trade sales; but branding spend was actually cut YoY to lift margins and the brand has not translated into pricing power.
BRAND.quote: We are positioned in the A category brand

INNOVATION.rationale: There are named product/process innovations — microfine GGBS for precast and high-performance concrete, WHRS, solar at Nandyal and Vijayanagar, and industry-best 258-268 kg CO2/ton with an 86/100 S&P CSA score — but no R&D spend is disclosed, no share-of-industry-R&D, and gross margins are commodity-level, so innovation is not funding dominance.
INNOVATION.quote: R&D led new product launches — Microfine GGBS with applications in precast and high performance concrete

FORWARD.rationale: The company sells 6,000+ direct customers and has an RMC business (INR574 crore FY26 revenue) plus advisory/testing services that move it toward the end user, but distribution is still overwhelmingly a 13,000-dealer wholesale network with no own-store, franchise or D2C economics discussed.
FORWARD.quote: RMC revenue is INR 574-odd crores. And for the quarter, it was INR 184 crores

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is explicit and repeated: 84% of India's GGBS market, Q1 FY26 volumes +7.8% vs ~3% industry, Q4 FY26 cement +12% vs 8% industry, and 2015-25 CAGRs of 12.96% capacity / 16.73% volume versus industry 4.77% / 6.15% — and it is being won on cost and green differentiation rather than reckless pricing, though the deliberate GGBS price restraint shows some share is being bought.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the industry growth in our markets was 8% Y-o-Y. And the cement volumes grew 12% in the same space, resulting, of course, in increasing market share

CULTURE.rationale: Promises made in Sep 2025 were delivered — Sambalpur commissioned that month, Nagaur commercial in March 2026, capex 'in line with the guidance we had given', cost savings tracked quarter by quarter — and bad news is disclosed promptly (Punjab EC delay, Dolvi slag shortage, soft April demand), with conservative accounting refusing to capitalise INR23 crore of branding spend; against this, leverage was 4.32x at listing and the listed track record is only one year.
CULTURE.quote: we prefer not doing things which are against the stated accounting norms... that's the prudent accounting policies that we follow

MOATTEST.rationale: The GGBS franchise has a genuinely hard-to-copy base — long-term contracted slag from co-located JSW Steel plants, 84% share, BIS/regulatory approvals for infra use, and 1.2bn MT of limestone across 12 mines — but the cement grinding business itself is buildable with capital, and the company's own Punjab EC delay shows permitting is a timing barrier, not a permanent one.
MOATTEST.quote: Secured the slag output from JSW Steel plants in South & West India... Grinding Units in South & West India co-located with JSW Steel plants

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 18 calls the discussion is one-off product sale through dealers/distributors — no licence fees, AMC, subscription, attach rates, renewals or deferred-revenue funding is ever mentioned.

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Management repeatedly describes painters and dealers as the recommending layer and invests in trade training (2,000 youth trained a year, Project Indradhanush), and dealer testimony on quality is cited as the key asset; but roughly half the buying occasion is consumer-led and the company spends heavily on celebrity consumer advertising, so the expert-gatekeeper lock-in is only partial.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: we use painters, largely 50% of the buying occasion is done through consumers and 50% through painters

TOLLROAD.rationale: Paint is a large, visible, negotiated line item for both retail and B2B customers — the FY26 calls describe excessive discounting, 12–18% price gaps versus a new entrant and forced price corrections, the opposite of a customer who pays without negotiating.
TOLLROAD.quote: there is excessive discounting happening in the market

LOWPRICE.rationale: The company is a sub-scale (#4) premium-priced player whose premium mix is mid-40s versus 22% for the industry; cost work exists (procurement, logistics, opex control) but the model is premium positioning being cut toward parity, not low-price-plus scale economics.
LOWPRICE.quote: premium contribution to our overall business is in mid -40s... whereas the market premium contribution is 22

PRICING.rationale: Early calls show calibrated increases (Aug 2022), but the trajectory is price deflation: a ~3% price drop in Dec 2023, admitted 5–9% over-pricing corrected in Sept–Oct 2025 and again in Jan–Feb 2026, and the May 2026 9.7% increase still lags ~13.5% RM inflation — pricing followed cost and competition rather than leading it.
PRICING.quote: we were usually overpriced between 5 % and 9 % which is what had led to volume erosion

BRAND.rationale: Dulux carries genuine heritage (70 years in India), rising brand-health scores, celebrity ambassadors and unmatched dealer quality perception, and A&P was guided from 2.5–3% up to 3.5–4%; but the brand did not convert into pricing power or sustained share — the premium had to be surrendered to defend volume.
BRAND.quote: there's no product which is close to Dulux in terms of quality

INNOVATION.rationale: Named launches recur every year with revenue commentary — Velvet Touch, Max PU exterior, FloorPlus, Simply Refresh DIY, VT Eterna, the FY26 luxury-finishes range — supported by a Bangalore colour/low-cost innovation centre; but R&D spend is never disclosed or quantified and the International Research Centre was carved out to the former parent in FY26, weakening the R&D-dominance claim.
INNOVATION.quote: we have launched VT Eterna, which is, in my view, the unbeatable interior paint

FORWARD.rationale: Some forward moves — direct e-commerce for Simply Refresh on Amazon, 16,000+ tinting machines placed with dealers, and post-acquisition integration of the projects/direct-sales model in 7 metros — but there is no own-store network, franchising or royalty stream; over 75% of paints turnover still routes through distributors.
FORWARD.quote: We are also selling it on Amazon.

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share-gain claims are made repeatedly (Nov 2024 'we continue to gain market share', FY26 23% blended volume growth, industrial wins like Navi Mumbai Airport and Porsche refinish), but 9M FY26 decorative volume growth was only 1–2%, the company sits at #4 chasing an 8% blended share, and recent volume was bought with price cuts that compressed EBITDA — exactly the low-quality share the pattern warns about.
SHAREGAIN.quote: as JSW Group in the paints business, I think we are already number four... we should get to number two in 3 to 4 years

CULTURE.rationale: Long-tenured operating leadership (Rajgopal since 2013, Krishna as CFO throughout), consistent quarterly investor engagement regardless of results, candid admission of mistakes (the 5–9% over-pricing, MEP weakness, October decline), and a conservative balance sheet with 5% working capital and net cash; offset by strategy discontinuity — the parent's portfolio review, divestment to JSW, and the admission that earlier EBITDA-percent pressure meant 'some of the actions were not sustained'.
CULTURE.quote: ever since I've taken over the role, we've continuously had investor engagements

MOATTEST.rationale: The 2024–26 calls show the advantage being removed in real time by a well-funded newcomer: Birla Opus entered at 12–18% lower effective prices and forced Dulux to cut premiums and lose volume, while JSW itself built a paints business from scratch — no time, data, R&D or location barrier is articulated that money could not rebuild.
MOATTEST.quote: You are talking of a new entrant which has come at prices which are anywhere up to 12% lower than the prices at which we operate

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue comes from long-term PPAs and capacity charges, not from a front-end product sale with an attached service/licence annuity; there is no discussion of attach rates, renewals or customer advances, and the model is the opposite of capital-light — ₹1,30,000 crore of planned capex to 2030 and net debt rising from ~₹26,500 crore (Dec-24) to ~₹62,000 crore (Sep-25) with 62-96 debtor days (positive working capital).
RECURRING.quote: We had earlier guided for a capital expenditure of ₹1,30,000 crore by 2030

TOLLROAD.rationale: Power is a large, negotiated line item for DISCOM off-takers, sold through reverse auctions and regulator-adopted tariffs — the opposite of an unnegotiated micro-cost; CERC even refused to adopt the BESS tariff JSW won as L1 in an e-reverse auction.
TOLLROAD.quote: JSW emerged as the L1 bidder in the e-Reverse auction

LOWPRICE.rationale: Repeated, itemised cost obsession across calls — coal sourced from nearby mines to cut logistics at KSK and Utkal, backward integration into blades/boilers/turbines for 'one of the lowest capital costs in the industry', WACD down 67bps to 8.36% — but this is a scale/asset-heavy utility with low asset turns, and price is set by auction rather than chosen as a strategy.
LOWPRICE.quote: building thermal capacity at one of the lowest capital costs in the industry

PRICING.rationale: Prices are set by regulators and competitive bidding, and the period shows deflation: day-ahead prices fell 26% YoY to ₹3.71/unit in Q3FY25 and averaged ₹3.86 through FY26; the only pricing edge cited is a ~20% premium to exchange prices from short-term contracting, not the ability to raise prices.
PRICING.quote: The day-ahead market prices have decreased 26% year-on-year to ₹3.71 per unit

INNOVATION.rationale: There are named new capability launches each year — agrivoltaics, first 20 MW floating solar, 3,800 TPA green hydrogen, a 5 GWh battery assembly plant that won a ₹440 crore external order — but no R&D spend is disclosed, and the core technology (boilers, turbines) is acquired from GE and Toshiba rather than developed.
INNOVATION.quote: we commissioned our first 20 MW floating solar project again at Vijayanagar

FORWARD.rationale: The integration runs the other way — backward into wind blades (Halol), boilers (GE Power), turbines (Toshiba JV stake raised to 10.7%), water/rail SPVs and battery assembly — while output still goes to DISCOMs and exchanges, with no own-channel or direct-customer economics.
FORWARD.quote: strengthening backward integration in the segment and supporting a lower LCOE

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified share gain across all seven calls: capacity 7.7 GW (Sep-24) to 14.6 GW (Q1FY27), generation +52%/+60%/+58% while national demand grew 0.9-3.3%, 47% of India's Q3FY25 wind additions, largest private hydro IPP, and thermal PLF 73-78% vs country 65.8-68.7%. The caveat the pattern warns about is live — the growth is debt- and equity-funded, with PAT down YoY in several quarters and leverage at ~5x.
SHAREGAIN.quote: a remarkable year-on-year growth of approximately 71%, up from 7.74 GW in the same period last year

CULTURE.rationale: Old-call promises are visibly delivered in later calls — the 10 GW-by-FY25 target, Kutehr commissioned in under six years, Tidong commissioned ahead of its October 2026 schedule, 36% of the FY27 3 GW guidance already achieved by Q1 — and bad news is disclosed promptly and specifically (₹16 crore quarterly curtailment loss, KSK PPA back-downs, weak Sutlej/Ravi hydrology, the CERC BESS tariff rejection, and the decision to pause solar module manufacturing). Leadership under Sharad Mahendra has been stable; the balance sheet, however, is levered rather than conservative.
CULTURE.quote: our decision to pause our solar module manufacturing plans

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-replicate assets — finite hydro sites (Karcham-Wangtoo, Baspa, Kutehr, Tidong), 26.4 GWh of pumped hydro, and scarce grid connectivity, which management calls a national bottleneck — plus KSK's ready balance-of-plant at below greenfield cost; but the sector added 64.9 GW in one year, so a well-funded entrant can replicate generation capacity itself.
MOATTEST.quote: a total connectivity, which we all are aware is a big challenge now in the country

RECURRING.rationale: Revenue is contracted and annuity-like — 30-year concessions, take-or-pay cargo commitments, and O&M contracts in UAE with minimum volume guarantees plus profit share — but there is no product-upfront-plus-service model, no attach/renewal-rate or deferred-revenue discussion, and the business is heavily capital-intensive rather than customer-funded.
RECURRING.quote: Slurry pipeline has already got t he take -or-pay agreement which will trigger from 1st of April '27

TOLLROAD.rationale: Port handling charges are a small fraction of the value of the steel, coal and iron ore moving through, and management repeatedly describes cargo as captive or sticky to the hinterland, with assured anchor cargo at Jatadhar; but there is no certification/standards or oligopoly-pricing language, and terminals are won through competitive bidding.
TOLLROAD.quote: most of the cargo is very sticky in natu re that it serves the hinterland is very -very close to the port area

PRICING.rationale: Q2 FY26 disclosed an explicit permanent rate increase at SWPL and Ennore worth Rs 27 crores with realisation per tonne up ~7% and port EBITDA margin rising to 53% from 52%, and margins have been steadily maintained above 50% across the nine calls; but tariffs are largely concession/bid-determined (Kolkata price discovery at Rs 4,678/TEU described as 'very competitive') so pricing is not freely raised above inflation.
PRICING.quote: Rs. 27 crores, it was primarily on account of a rate increase we have taken in SWPL as well as in Ennore Coal Terminal. So, this is a permanent rate increase

FORWARD.rationale: Consistent multi-year push down the chain toward the end customer: container train operator licence (Nov 2023), Navkar acquisition (2024, now profitable), NCR Rail via NCLT and the Kudathini multimodal park (2025), building toward an Rs 8,000 crore pan-India logistics top line by FY30 — but this is logistics integration, not own-store/franchise/D2C economics.
FORWARD.quote: we were never into end-mile delivery. So this is the first step towards the connecting the end customer directly

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Persistent, quantified share gain across all nine calls: capacity from 170 to 177 mtpa today with a stated path to 288 by FY28 and 400 by FY30, third-party share rising 36% → 46% → 52%, plus wins at Murbe, Keni, Jatadhar, Kolkata Berth 7/8 and acquisitions (Fujairah, PNP, Navkar, NCR Rail) — and management stresses the 16% project-IRR hurdle rather than buying volume.
SHAREGAIN.quote: the share of third -party increased to 46% in the overall mix from 36% a n year ago

CULTURE.rationale: Positives are real — conservative balance sheet through the period (net cash in FY25, net debt/EBITDA only 0.75x by Sep 2025), upgrade to investment grade by S&P and Fitch, orderly CEO/CFO succession, and candid quantification of misses (the 3.4 mt Paradip iron ore shortfall, Jaigarh/Dharamtar declines) — but delivery has slipped against the 'we deliver what we commit' claim: Jaigarh LPG moved from Jan '26 to June '26 to FY27-end, Tuticorin slipped a quarter, and the reaffirmed 10% volume guidance came in at 4-5% through H1 FY26.
CULTURE.quote: we have delivered all our projects on time, whatever we have committed to the market in the last several years, we have done that

MOATTEST.rationale: The replication barrier is concrete and repeatedly evidenced: finite coastal locations held under 30-year concessions, multi-year regulatory gauntlets (EIA, public hearings at Keni and Murbe stretching across several calls), billions of rupees of dredging and berth capex, and captive JSW Steel anchor cargo plus a dedicated 302 km slurry pipeline — none of which a funded newcomer could assemble in a few years.
MOATTEST.quote: JSW Infrastructure stands out as the only port company in India currently engaged in the simultaneous development of three greenfield ports

TOLLROAD.rationale: Steel is a large, closely negotiated input for JSW's customers, not a sub-1% critical spend — auto contracts are repriced quarterly and domestic prices track imports, the opposite of toll-road pricing indifference.
TOLLROAD.quote: auto gets recalibrated quarterly. So , the pric e increase for automotive will come in this quarter

LOWPRICE.rationale: Management repeatedly emphasises low specific investment cost, high asset utilisation (96% Indian capacity, 95% downstream), digitalisation/AI-driven reliability and logistics optimisation of captive ore sourcing — a genuine cost culture, but there is no evidence of deliberately passing savings into price to win volume.
LOWPRICE.quote: with our faster pace of execution and low specific invest ment cost, we are well plac ed to grow in India

PRICING.rationale: Pricing is commodity- and policy-determined, not company-determined: April '26 realisations are merely back to April '23 levels, the recovery is attributed to a safeguard duty, and management concedes international prices govern domestic ones.
PRICING.quote: internationa l prices will always be a guiding factor for the domestic steel prices

BRAND.rationale: Branded retail and value-added share are managed as a mix lever — branded sales ~50% of retail sales and a stated intent to hold VASP above 50% — but there is no heritage story, A&P spend, or premium pricing evidence on the call.
BRAND.quote: branded sales constituted about 50% of our total retail sales, enhancing the overall value of the volumes

INNOVATION.rationale: Product-mix upgrading (CRGO, electrical steel, tinplate, special engineering steel) plus digitalisation/AI is real, but the key technologies are imported through JV partners rather than generated by disclosed in-house R&D, and no R&D spend is quantified.
INNOVATION.quote: POSCO also has their own areas of technology and especially i n the high -strength steels, giga steels

FORWARD.rationale: JSW One, the 61%-owned digital distribution platform, turned profitable in Q4 with GMV up 57% to Rs.6,200 crores and embedded credit — a genuine move toward the end customer — alongside branded retail, though own-store/franchise economics are absent.
FORWARD.quote: The steel volumes gr ew by 50% Y oY and the GMV reached Rs.6,200 cror es, a 57% YoY increase

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Explicit, quantified outgrowth of the industry — 12% volume growth against 8% industry demand in FY26, with FY27 guidance of 10% sales / 13% production growth ex-BPSL and capacity rising to 62mt by FY32 — and management commits to sustaining ~1.5x industry growth.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have no doubt that about 10% to 12% of market sales growth for JSW would b e a challenge on those lines. So , we are quite confident on that

CULTURE.rationale: Delivery against stated guidance is verifiable (99% of production, 102% of sales guidance) and the balance-sheet promise was kept — Rs.30,000 crores of the Rs.37,000 crores BPSL deleveraging done, with leverage caps voluntarily tightened from 3.75x to 3.0x — but the record is judged from a single call and sits against a Rs.2.26 lakh crore capex commitment.
CULTURE.quote: We achieved 99% of our production guidance and 102% of our sales vo lume guidance for the year

MOATTEST.rationale: Real replication barriers exist — 25 iron ore mines with 1.7bn tonnes of resources, Mozambique coking coal, the world's largest single-location plant and 4-5 year project lead times — but these are capital and licence barriers in a commodity, not a durable pricing moat.
MOATTEST.quote: Any capacity which you set up today takes 4 to 5 years minimum

RECURRING.rationale: Across all 16 calls the revenue model is purely transactional QSR order revenue — no licence fees, AMC, subscription or deferred-revenue funding is ever discussed; the closest analogue, Cheesy Rewards loyalty (25mn members, >50% of business), is repeat purchase, not contracted recurring revenue.
RECURRING.quote: serving more than three crore customer orders in this quarter

MIDDLEMAN.rationale: Sales are direct to end consumers via own app, delivery and dine-in, with brand marketing and loyalty as the acquisition engine; no professional/prescriber intermediary appears anywhere in the record.
MIDDLEMAN.quote: record high MAU at 12.1 million which was up by 17.5% yoy

TOLLROAD.rationale: JFL is a consumer-facing restaurant operator, not a critical small-share input supplier; there is no certification, standards or 'customers don't switch' language in any call.

LOWPRICE.rationale: Repeated across the years: eight straight quarters of no price increase while absorbing record inflation via the 'Vijay' productivity programme, free delivery and MOV cut to Rs.99, Rs.99 Lunch Thali and Rs.49-79 price points aimed at idli/dosa occasions, plus a cost culture that cut capex per store ~20% a year for three years — all funded by scale (3,600 stores) and high gross margins.
LOWPRICE.quote: we didn't take any price increase since the last eight quarters and absorbed cost inflation through internal cost optimization and productivity enhancement program – Vijay

PRICING.rationale: The multi-year trajectory is the opposite of pricing power: two-year price freeze while cheese hit 10-year highs (Nov 2022, Aug 2024), free delivery and a forced cut of minimum order value from Rs.149 to Rs.99 to match aggregators, and in May 2026 only ~120bps of pricing against ~120bps of energy inflation alone plus labour and commodity headwinds; the recent 'calibrated' increases and premium launches are a partial offset, not demonstrated pricing power.
PRICING.quote: we have very consciously taken a call to reduce minimum order value from Rs.149 to Rs. 99... as a result, there was a drop in the average ticket size

BRAND.rationale: Real brand salience — 'It Happens Only with Pizza' refresh lifting brand scores, ~2/3 share of the pizza category, loyalty stickiness, and stretch into Popeyes/COFFY/Hong's — but the core brand is licensed from Domino's rather than owned heritage, and brand strength has not converted into premium pricing (see the price freeze and MOV cut).
BRAND.quote: The brand-refresh It Happens Only with Pizza helped us significantly improve our brand scores

INNOVATION.rationale: Every call names new products with stated commercial impact — East India regional range and no-onion-no-garlic (2022), Cheese Volcano, Rs.99 Lunch Thali, Chillrz (2024), Big Big Pizza, Sourdough and Cheese Lava Pull Apart (2026) explicitly called gross-margin accretive — alongside sustained tech/AI and micro-services investment funded by ~75% gross margins; no formal R&D line is disclosed, which is the only gap.
INNOVATION.quote: Our recent new product launches, including Sourdough Pizza and Cheese Lava Pull Apart, have seen an overwhelming response... these products are accretive to gross margin

FORWARD.rationale: The whole model is forward-integrated manufacturing: own commissaries feeding ~2,530 own stores in India, own-app D2C with 76% delivery mix and own-asset share of delivery pushed to record highs, its own delivery fleet, plus an asset-light franchise engine in Turkey where 88% of stores are franchisee-run and JFL earns revenue serving them.
FORWARD.quote: 88% of the Turkey store network is franchisee-operated, which makes the model asset-lite

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Consistent, quantified share gain: store network from 1,701 Domino's India stores (2022) to ~2,530 (2026) with 1,000 more planned in three years, ~2/3 pizza category share, and a 50,000-customer AC Nielsen panel confirming gains in pizza and across bowls/chicken/burgers; the caveat is that some of it was bought with free delivery and a lower MOV that diluted ticket size.
SHAREGAIN.quote: we have gained share, and we have gained share materially in pizza as a category

CULTURE.rationale: Promoter family (Bhartias) has been stable through the whole record, promises were kept — 250-store guidance (2022), the gross-margin improvement flagged '3 or 4 earnings calls ago' delivered in FY26, Turkey now self-servicing acquisition debt — and management openly names dine-in as 'the real challenge to solve'; offsetting this, an analyst pushed back hard in May 2026 on refusal to quantify margin guidance, and the CEO's tenure is only ~4 years.
CULTURE.quote: we had actually mentioned, if you recall in our earnings call about 3 or 4 earnings calls ago that we'll improve the gross margin

MOATTEST.rationale: There is a genuine, articulable barrier — the exclusive Domino's India master franchise, a multi-temperature commissary network built ahead of the curve, ~2,530 stores giving 20-minute delivery in 427 cities, and the fixed-cost density that makes it work — which a funded entrant could not rebuild quickly; but the moat is visibly contestable, as aggregators forced JFL to match a Rs.99 MOV and it cannot pass through energy inflation.
MOATTEST.quote: we are building a 5,000-store business that is most penetrated, and I believe these are actually barriers to acquiring customers

TOLLROAD.rationale: Several products are small-but-critical inputs to customers (advanced agro/pharma intermediates made on innovators' proprietary technology, vitamin B3 in feed/cosmetics), and the Aug-2022 call argued their products survive customer energy crises because energy content of the finished product is low; certification anchoring (USFDA audit of Bharuch, 20+ customer quality/EHS audits in Q1 FY27) supports the switching-cost story, but there is no evidence of oligopoly pricing discipline — acetyls and choline pricing is openly commoditised.
TOLLROAD.quote: the contribution of energy costs to the finished product is not very large which is affecting the overall consumption

LOWPRICE.rationale: There is a genuine, itemised cost culture — Rs.120 crore of annualised lean savings mobilised by FY25 and again delivered in FY26, a Rs.100 crore FY27 target, working capital cut from 89 to ~59 days — but savings are retained in margin rather than passed to price, and the strategy is portfolio premiumisation, not low-price scale.
LOWPRICE.quote: we achieved Rs. 120 crore lean savings

PRICING.rationale: Across the four years management describes cost pass-through and market-set prices, not price rises above cost inflation: coal costs only 'partly' passed on in FY23, acetic anhydride and choline prices repeatedly 'under pressure' from imports through FY25, and in May 2026 the CEO named pricing as the assumption that broke the Pinnacle plan.
PRICING.quote: one big assumption which I keep calling out is the pricing, which has surprised all of us

INNOVATION.rationale: A regular cadence of named launches with revenue impact (Diketene, food-grade choline chloride and choline bitartrate, GMP food/cosmetic-grade B3, 20+ personal care products in development) plus a CDMO/fine chemicals funnel of 100+ molecules worth Rs.3,500 crore peak revenue and a dedicated semicon R&D/clean room; however R&D spend is never quantified or benchmarked against the industry.
INNOVATION.quote: We have a funnel of 100-plus molecules with INR3,500-plus crore of peak revenue potential

FORWARD.rationale: The Remidex Pharma acquisition (FY26) is an explicit move down the chain from discrete molecules into premixes and finished human-nutrition solutions for existing customers; but there are no own stores, franchising or D2C economics — this is B2B forward integration only.
FORWARD.quote: the idea of acquiring this business is to forward integrate into that segment

SHAREGAIN.rationale: Share gain is claimed and repeated with specifics across all 20 calls: Acetic Anhydride domestic leadership plus rising European share from Aug-2022 through FY26, global #1 in pyridine/picoline as the only scaled non-Chinese player, and export mix rising from 38% to 48% of revenue between Q2 FY24 and Q2 FY25 — gains made while margins improved (Specialty EBITDA margin 27% held six quarters), not bought.
SHAREGAIN.quote: We are now globally #1 player in Pyridine and Picolines and the only scaled non-Chinese player

CULTURE.rationale: The record shows promises kept — Bharuch CDMO plant built in 14 months and the $300mn agro contract shipping in March 2026 'as we had promised', Rs.120 crore savings delivered, net debt/EBITDA down to 0.99x, guidance deliberately not upgraded on a strong Q1 — and bad news is disclosed promptly (coal hit quantified at Rs.45 crore, catalyst change, pricing assumption missed); against that, the flagship Pinnacle 345 vision has quietly slipped from five years to four with the shortfall unquantified.
CULTURE.quote: The project actually started in March, as we had promised to all of you

MOATTEST.rationale: Some genuinely hard-to-replicate assets — sole scaled non-Chinese pyridine chain, regulator- and customer-audited GMP/USFDA sites, WEF Global Manufacturing Lighthouse, multi-year contracts embedding an innovator's proprietary process — but the core acetyls and choline lines are demonstrably replicable, with Chinese imports repeatedly compressing choline and niacinamide prices, so the moat does not cover the portfolio.
MOATTEST.quote: the demand for choline remains stable, although the pricing pressure continued due to high imports
